oneLiner.en: On Lag BaOmer, the Rema's yahrzeit, the Mashgiach suggests that the Rema is the revealed side of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai: Rabbi Shimon used the dove and revealed the hidden good in every Jew and even in the tochacha, while the Rema used the raven to uncover what is not in order.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a feeling that the Rema, whose yahrzeit is Lag BaOmer and who is the Rebbe of Ashkenazi Jewry, is the revealed part of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. He tells how the Maggid of Mezritch smelled chametz at his seder because the Baal HaTanya had kashered a glass cup against the Rema's view, and the Rema came to complain. He then tells how the Rema, as a new rav, exposed a seller of non-kosher fat by seeing ravens over his wagon. Rabbi Shimon, by contrast, answered his students by a dove that everything in the tochacha is blessing. The Mashgiach explains that every Jew is a letter of the Torah holding a secret, that the tochacha hides the secret of the geulah, and that on Lag BaOmer every Jew can find himself in Rabbi Shimon. He closes with Rabbi Shimon's promise that the Torah will not be forgotten.

en: The Mashgiach suggests, as a feeling of his own, that the Rema is the revealed (nigleh) part of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, and that both share Lag BaOmer.
Rabbi Shimon worked with the dove, which brings good tidings, while the Rema worked with the raven, which reveals what is wrong.
Every Jew corresponds to a letter of the Sefer Torah and adds something no other Jew can add, so even the simplest Jew holds a hidden secret.
The tochacha hides the secret of the geulah, and its letters too are Jewish souls.
On Lag BaOmer, even at its lowest level, every Jew can find himself in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.

catalogTitle: The נסים in Current Events

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in the last generation, like in the month of Adar, Hashem hides Himself and works His nissim within nature, and the Megillah teaches how to find His hand in the events of our own day.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the structure of 248 limbs, from the skull to the heel, found in man, in the Torah's 248 positive mitzvos, in history and in geography. The first generation, of the Exodus and Matan Torah, is the head; the last generation, ikvesa d'Meshicha, is the heel, the darkest part of the body, and he is convinced it is ours. The calendar too runs from Nisan, the month of revealed nissim, down to Adar, whose name means a cloak. Haman rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar, and especially in Adar Sheni, an appendage like the last eight pesukim of the Torah, written in tears. He did not know that history moves in a circle: after Adar comes Nisan, and the last generation becomes the head. The Megillah has no open nissim and not even Hashem's name; its nissim are hidden in nature, as the Bnei Yissaschar's parable and the chain of Purim events show. Reading the Megillah this way, the Mashgiach says, one can read today's news and see Hashem pulling the strings.

en: The structure of 248 limbs, from head to heel, appears in man, in the mitzvos, in history and in geography.
The first generation, which saw the Exodus and Matan Torah, is the head; the last generation, ikvesa d'Meshicha, is the heel, and the Mashgiach is convinced it is ours.
Nisan is the month of revealed nissim, while Adar, meaning a cloak, is the month in which Hashem conceals Himself.
Haman's mistake was to see history as a straight line; it is a circle, and after Adar comes Nisan.
The Megillah has no supernatural nissim and does not mention Hashem's name; its nissim are hidden within nature.
The Megillah is an exercise in finding Hashem between the words, and one who reads it correctly can see Him conducting today's events too.

title.en: From head to heel: man, history, geography

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the structure of 248 limbs, from the skull to the heel, in man, in the 248 positive mitzvos, in the generations and in the places of the world. The first generation is the head and ours, the heel of Moshiach, is the last, but since the line is a circle the last generation will become the head again.

title.en: Nisan and Adar: revelation and concealment

summary.en: The calendar runs from Nisan, when the first generation saw Hashem's nissim, down to Adar, whose name means a cloak. Haman rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar, thinking Hashem makes no nissim then; the Mashgiach brings the Gemara's source for Esther in the Torah, Hashem hiding His face, and the Yerushalmi that the Purim miracle happened in Adar Sheni.

title.en: Appendages: the Torah's last letters and Adar Sheni

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Torah's 600,000 letters correspond to 600,000 Jewish souls, and that the last eight pesukim, written by Moshe in tears, are an appendage to the Torah, as Adar Sheni is to the calendar. Haman thought the mazal of Adar was death, but did not know that the circle starts over.

title.en: Hidden nissim: the Bnei Yissaschar's parable

summary.en: The Mashgiach says our heel generation lives in a sea of hatred of Jews, yet Hashem's hand is visible as in the Megillah, which has no open nissim and not even His name. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar's parable of a dying patient whose medicine from China and doctor from America arrive at the last moment, to explain nissim within nature.

title.en: Everything just in time in the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the chain of events in the Megillah, from the feast of Achashverosh and Vashti's death to Bigsan and Seresh and Charbona's words, each insignificant alone but together a nes. He brings the Chiddushei HaRim's parable of a yeshiva that would have dismissed the news of Vashti as idle talk, and says today's events may yet be part of a future Megillah.

title.en: Reading the news like the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Hashem's name is hidden in the crevices of the Megillah and must be searched for. With a parable of a marionette show, he says the world's leaders are puppets on invisible strings, and that one who reads the Megillah correctly can see Hashem's name in the New York Times.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains, through the parsha of the kings of Edom, that the vessels broke because the receivers said "I will rule" instead of submitting to the giver, and that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the secret of the Yovel, repairs this breakage and brings it down to the lowest souls of the last generations.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the joy of Lag BaOmer, which grows from generation to generation because the higher a light is, the lower it reaches. He turns to the parsha of the kings who ruled in Edom, which, as the sefer he reads explains, holds the whole plan of how Hashem runs the world, where in the end kedushah alone will rule. Following the Arizal, he explains that all of creation is giver and receiver; the vessels broke because the receivers said "I will rule", and the sparks fell into the sitra achra. Raising those sparks back to their root is Yovel. Rabbi Shimon, the secret of fifty, descends to the lowest level to repair our souls, and Lag BaOmer is the repair of the breakage. The Mashgiach closes with the love among Rabbi Shimon's companions, the circle of dancers, and Rabbi Shimon's view that all Jews are princes.

en: The joy of Lag BaOmer grows from generation to generation, because the higher a light is, the lower it descends.
The parsha of the kings of Edom contains the whole plan of Hashem's running of the world, whose end is that kedushah alone will rule.
All of creation works as giver and receiver; the vessels broke because the receivers did not submit to the giver but said "I will rule".
A Jew's task is to raise the sparks trapped in the sitra achra, for example by eating with kedushah, and bringing them back to their root is called Yovel.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the secret of fifty, descends to the lowest level to repair the souls of the last generations; Lag BaOmer is the repair of the breakage of "I will rule".
According to Rabbi Shimon all Jews are princes and all are equal, and in the days of Moshiach the halacha will follow him.

title.en: The joy of Lag BaOmer grows each generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Lag BaOmer as the day of joy, honored by tzaddikim above other days, and tells that Reb Moshe of Rozvadov could not part from it. He says the joy grows with each generation, because the higher a thing is, the lower it reaches.

title.en: The kings of Edom and the plan of creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from a sefer on the parsha of the kings who ruled in Edom: seven kings are followed by "and he died", while the eighth has no death and his wife's name is given. The sefer explains that this small parsha holds the whole way Hashem runs the world, the struggle of kedushah and tumah, whose end is that kedushah alone will rule; the Mashgiach adds that nothing ever happens against Hashem's will.

title.en: A secret hidden in the parsha

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Moshe hid the secret of the whole creation in this parsha so that only the worthy would see it, and that great tzaddikim like Rabbi Shimon and his companions had a grasp of it, with many pages of Zohar on it. In exile the sitra achra holds power and the great lights are hidden; he then introduces the explanation that chassidishe seforim bring from the Arizal.

title.en: Giver and receiver, and the breaking of the vessels

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that all of creation is giver and receiver, like man and wife and Hashem and Klal Yisroel. The first vessels were too close to the great lights and did not submit to the giver but said "I will rule", so they broke and sparks fell into the sitra achra; a Jew raises them by eating, dressing and doing business with kedushah, and he explains why a table is called shulchan.

title.en: Yovel: returning the sparks to their root

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that raising the sparks and returning them to their root is called Yovel. Our time is the level of hod shebehod, the lowest part of creation, and Rabbi Shimon descends to it as the one who gathers all the camps, which is why later generations feel more light on Lag BaOmer; he is the secret of fifty and the repair of "I will rule".

title.en: The eighth king, Shavuos, and believing

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Lag BaOmer is the repair of the breakage: the eighth king, whose wife is named, stands for a receiver that does not break. He speaks of the last third of the Sefirah as the preparation for Shavuos, tells of the Kotzker's reply that believing is greater than seeing, and blesses the listeners; a gap in the recording follows.

title.en: Lag BaOmer grows as night falls

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Lag BaOmer reaches down to the lowest level: unlike other Yamim Tovim, it grows greater as the day turns to night, until midnight or the next day's count, because this Yom Tov comes down to us. He urges taking strength from Rabbi Shimon; the stretch ends in singing.

title.en: The love of the chevraya and the dancing circle

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the great love among Rabbi Shimon's companions, who followed Rabbi Akiva's teaching on loving one's fellow, and the instruction that the companions hold hands in a closed circle like an electric circuit. He says he has often protested against letting go of hands or talking in the middle of a dance, since that breaks the bond.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon is Shabbos; all Jews are princes

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that as there is a time and a place that are Shabbos, Rabbi Shimon is the soul that is Shabbos, and brings the Divrei Yoel that in the days of Moshiach the halacha will follow him. He explains Rabbi Shimon's view that all Jews are princes and all equal, alluded to in "the valley of Shaveh", and closes with a blessing for all who are bound to Rabbi Shimon.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of yovel, the gathering of all of Klal Yisroel into one, and that this is why the hair, which stands for the dinim of Esav, may be cut at the upsherin on Lag BaOmer.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of yovel, the fiftieth gate, when all Jewish souls flow together into one, as at Har Sinai and in the love among his chaverim; this is why Meron gathers more Jews than any place in the world. He then explains that every portion of Eretz Yisroel matches a halachah of the Torah, bringing the Gemara on Osniel ben Kenaz and the Ba'al Shem Tov's reversed reading, so that a young man finishing Shas on this day draws down the whole of Eretz Yisroel. A story of Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir shows how the geulah may come. In the second half he explains the upsherin: hair is dinim, linked to Esav, the hairy man of Har Seir, which may not be touched until Moshiach; Rabbi Shimon, an aspect of Moshiach, allows it, as the fourth year of orlah is holy.

en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of yovel and the fiftieth gate, where all Jewish souls join into one soul.
The gathering of Jews at Meron, the largest gathering of Jews in the world, is a taste of the ingathering of yovel and of the final redemption.
Every portion of Eretz Yisroel corresponds to a halachah of the Torah, so the whole Torah is the whole of Eretz Yisroel, and finishing Shas draws down all of it.
Hair represents dinim and is bound to Esav, the hairy man of Har Seir, which cannot be touched until the time of Moshiach.
Because Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is an aspect of Moshiach, on his day the hair may be cut, like the fourth year of orlah whose fruit is holy.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai as yovel

summary.en: The Mashgiach says this year is a yovel year and that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of yovel and the fiftieth gate, when all Jewish souls flow together. He ties it to the unity at Har Sinai, the love among Rabbi Shimon's chaverim, and the great gathering of Jews at Meron.

title.en: Eretz Yisroel, the Torah and a siyum

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every portion of Eretz Yisroel matches a halachah, bringing the Gemara on Osniel ben Kenaz and the Ba'al Shem Tov's reversed reading. A young man finishing Shas on Lag BaOmer therefore draws down the whole land, and he tells of Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir and how the geulah may come.

title.en: Sefirah, hair and the dinim of Esav

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the 49 days of sefirah as a thirst for Elokim, and turns to the custom of upsherin. He explains that hair is dinim, bound to Esav and Har Seir, which may not be touched until the time of Moshiach, and that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is an aspect of Moshiach.

title.en: Milah, orlah and the fall of Esav

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the three orlos of milah and priah from the Bnei Yissaschar, the Ben Yehoyada on the sons of Keturah and the Tanya on the source of the body. He then ties the three years of uncut hair to the three years of orlah, the fourth year being holy, and describes Lag BaOmer as the fall of Esav, from which chessed leads to the fiftieth day.

title.en: Untranscribed stretch and garbled close

summary.en: Almost nine minutes in which only a few words were transcribed, followed by a short, heavily garbled close in which the Mashgiach speaks about a brachah someone gave.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Lag Baomer, the day Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed the secrets of the Torah, reveals the hidden point of holiness in every Jew, even the lowliest, and that each Jew must bring his own hidden 'secret' into the open.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a Zohar: the 25 letters of Shema correspond to the higher unity, which Moshe completed, while Yaakov could only complete the 24 letters of Baruch Shem, since there was no Mishkan yet; the verse about the Ohel Moed has 25 letters. Together they make 49, like the days of the Omer, after which the fiftieth, the Yovel, is revealed. Counting Baruch Shem first, the 33rd letter is the first yud of Hashem's name in Shema, so on Lag Baomer the 'tip of the yud', the point in every Jew, is revealed; this is the repair of the lowly. Answering why one rejoices on a yahrzeit, he brings the Pri Tzaddik on 'Yaakov did not die': in pshat he died, in the higher levels he lives. Moshe gave the pshat; Rabbi Shimon revealed the sod, where there is no death. After singing, he explains the sin of Rabbi Akiva's students: each Jew is a letter of the Torah with a hidden sod, and Lag Baomer calls on each to reveal it, preparing for Matan Torah.

en: The 25 letters of Shema and the 24 of Baruch Shem together make 49, corresponding to the days of the Omer, after which the fiftieth level, the Yovel, is revealed.
Counting Baruch Shem first, the 33rd letter is the first yud of Hashem's name in Shema, so Lag Baomer reveals the 'tip of the yud', the point that every Jew has.
Lag Baomer is the repair of the lowly, because every Jew is bound to that point, which no one can destroy.
Moshe gave the Torah's laws and its plain meaning, while Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a reincarnation of Moshe, revealed its secrets, and in the realm of sod there is no death.
Every Jew is a letter in the Torah and carries a hidden sod that no other Jew has; on Lag Baomer he must bring it to revelation, as a preparation for Matan Torah.

Once the Mishkan was built, 25 letters became possible, as the 25 letters of the verse about the Ohel Moed show; together the letters make 49.

title.en: Lag Baomer and the tip of the yud

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the 49 letters correspond to the Omer, after which the Yovel is revealed, and that Lag Baomer is the repair of the lowly. Counting Baruch Shem first, the 33rd letter is the first yud of Hashem's name, so on Lag Baomer the tip of the yud, the point in every Jew from the greatest to the smallest, is revealed.

title.en: Simcha on a yahrzeit: Yaakov did not die

summary.en: The Mashgiach cites the Pri Chadash and the Chasam Sofer, who wonder how one may rejoice on Rabbi Shimon's yahrzeit, and the Yismach Moshe's response. He answers with the Pri Tzaddik on the Gemara 'Yaakov Avinu did not die': the four levels of Torah correspond to worlds, and in the world of pshat Yaakov died, while his root in drush lives on.

title.en: Moshe gave pshat, Rabbi Shimon revealed sod

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Moshe gave the laws and plain meaning, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a reincarnation of Moshe, revealed the Torah's secrets; in that realm he did not die. On Lag Baomer a Jew rejoices in his own point of sod, and the Mashgiach notes that both Yaakov and Rabbi Shimon passed away with the word 'chaim', life.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing of Lag Baomer songs, including Bar Yochai; the transcript here is fragments of the lyrics and noise.

title.en: Every Jew carries a hidden sod

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Rabbi Akiva's students needed to honor one another when one was greater than the other, and answers that each Jew is a letter in the Torah with a hidden sod that no one else has. Lag Baomer, the day of revealing secrets, calls on every Jew to bring his own sod into the open as preparation for Matan Torah; he closes with a blessing.

catalogTitle: A New יו”ט for Each Generation

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim is a new Yom Tov in every generation: Hashem hides behind nature, yet the Megillah's miracles are renewed each year, and Purim calls for bitachon against the fear and the 'coincidence' thinking of Amalek.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by calling Purim a great, misunderstood day that the Zohar compares to Yom Kippur, and says it should give Jews bitachon in current events. Purim is a Yom Tov of galus; the Jews then sinned by joining Achashverosh's feast, which celebrated his calculation that the seventy years had passed with no Beis Hamikdash. Unlike Pesach, Purim brings new miracles in every generation, hidden behind hester panim, the concealment of Hashem's face, which he finds today in the new Israeli government, global fear and weakened Yiddishkeit. Haman's power was fear; Mordechai and Esther answered it with bitachon. Citing the Arizal and the Chasam Sofer, he explains that the Megillah's light is greater because it came to a generation that had fallen so low. Purim is the reverse of Yom Kippur: the Shechinah descends to us. Finally he explains three meanings of Amalek's 'korcha', ending with Amalek's denial of hashgachah pratis and the historian Graetz's 'natural' account of the splitting of the sea.

en: Purim is not a one-time miracle like the Exodus; every year and every generation has its own new Purim and its own new Megillah.
Purim is a day of hester: Hashem hides, but He watches from behind the wall, and every detail of the Megillah and of current events is part of the miracle.
The main avodah of Purim is bitachon; Haman's power was to spread fear, and Mordechai and Esther overcame it by trusting Hashem.
The Megillah's light is greater because it was given at the end of the seventy years, in a time of ikvesa d'Meshicha and intermarriage like today; a deep pit needs a stronger light.
Yom Kippur and Purim share one purpose but work in opposite ways: on Yom Kippur Jews rise to Hashem, on Purim the Shechinah comes down to them in their lowliness.
Amalek's 'korcha' means he made the Jews impure, made them cold, and above all taught that everything is chance; Jews believe there is no such thing as coincidence.

title.en: Purim, a great Yom Tov of galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is a misunderstood, very great day that the Zohar compares to Yom Kippur, and that it should give bitachon in current events. Purim is a Yom Tov of galus, and he explains the sin of joining Achashverosh's feast, which celebrated his calculation that the Beis Hamikdash would never be rebuilt.

title.en: A new Purim in every generation; today's hester

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Purim is a new Yom Tov for each generation, with a rerun of its miracles every year, and that every family and town has its Purim. Purim is hester, as the Gemara finds Esther in 'haster astir panai'; he describes today's hester in the new Israeli government's war on the chareidim and in the global fear.

title.en: Hashem peeks through the cracks

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how in a yeshiva class of about a hundred boys only one said Shir HaShirim before Shabbos, a sign of watered-down Yiddishkeit and itself part of the hester. Yet Hashem watches through the cracks, every detail of the Megillah and of today is part of the miracle, a Megillah is being written now, and the avodah is bitachon for the coming weeks.

title.en: Haman's fear and Esther's bitachon

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Haman's main klipah was spreading fear, and brings the child's passuk to Mordechai, 'do not fear sudden terror'. This year's double Adar is the month of decision; Mordechai did not bow, and Esther, feeling the Shechinah leave her, cried 'Keli Keli lama azavtani' and went to the king with mesirus nefesh and bitachon.

title.en: Why the Megillah's light is greater

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every year's events can be found in the Megillah, and brings the Chasam Sofer's Drashos that the light of Megillas Esther is greater than that of the Torah of Moshe. He explains it: the Megillah came at the end of the seventy years, in an ikvesa d'Meshicha full of intermarriage like today, and a deep pit needs a stronger light.

title.en: A new light: the Megillah of every year

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Arizal that the kedushah of Purim was a new revelation of Hashem never seen before, an 'ohr chadash', so each year's Megillah is new. One who reads it as an old story has not fulfilled the mitzvah, and the Megillah will remain in the days of Moshiach because its real story will be the last Purim before the geulah.

title.en: Yom Kippur rises, Purim descends; Amalek's chill

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Yom Kippur, when Jews rise to the heavens, with Purim, when the Shechinah comes down to them, all the more in Adar Sheni, which trails behind the camp like those Amalek attacked. He then explains 'asher korcha' as Amalek making the Jews impure and making them cold, without fire in learning and davening.

title.en: Amalek denies hashgachah pratis

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains a third meaning of 'korcha': Amalek denies hashgachah pratis, the first of the Rambam's principles. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's teaching on a falling leaf and warns that even one sentence of kefirah leaves a mark that takes years to remove.

title.en: Graetz and the splitting of the sea

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how as a boy he opened Graetz's history of the Jews and found it admits the splitting of the sea as a historical fact, witnessed by a whole nation. All the nations were frightened by it except Aluf Amalek, and Graetz explained it away as a natural event of tides and weather.

title.en: No coincidence: the Megillah's string of pearls

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers Graetz that such timing would itself be a greater miracle, like the miracle of the Megillah. Amalek, like Graetz, sees everything as natural chance, while Jews know there is no coincidence; Purim teaches emunah that every passuk of the Megillah is a pearl on one string, natural events over which we bless 'she'asah nissim'.

catalogTitle: תיקון פגימת הלבנה ע”י טובת עין

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the flaw of the moon, born of its jealousy, is repaired by a good eye: through the leap year's thirteenth month, through Esther becoming queen, and through Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's thirteenth year in the cave and his teaching of love between friends.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach starts from the seven 'ro'ei pnei hamelech' in the Megillah. Following the Gemara and the Chasam Sofer, their names allude to korbanos, so the angels above with the same names pleaded for the Jews. Rashi reads them as the heavenly angels busy with the leap year so that Esther would become queen. Why would angels deal with a leap year? Because the leap year repairs the flaw of the moon, which was diminished for envying the sun. Esther is the moon, and her kingship is the moon's repair. The repair is a good eye: the students of Rabbi Akiva lacked it, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a gilgul of Shimon who led the sale of Yosef, fixed it with his thirteenth year in the cave and his teaching of 'hinei mah tov'. Lag BaOmer and Purim, which fall on the same weekday, share this tikkun.

en: The seven ministers' names allude to korbanos, so the seven angels above with the same names pleaded for the Jews, as the Chasam Sofer explains.
According to Rashi, the 'knowers of the times' were the heavenly angels, who busied themselves with the leap year so that Esther would become queen and the Jews would be saved.
The leap year is a repair of the moon's flaw: the thirteenth month makes up the days by which the moon falls behind the sun.
The moon was diminished because it lacked a good eye toward the sun, and this jealousy runs through history, from the sin of the Tree of Knowledge to the sale of Yosef.
Esther is the moon, and her becoming queen is the repair of the moon's flaw.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a gilgul of Shimon who led the sale of Yosef, repaired it with a good eye and with love between friends.

title.en: Opening, mostly untranscribed

summary.en: The first minutes of the recording are almost entirely missing from the transcript; only a fragment about numbers in the pesukim survives.

title.en: The seven ministers and the seven angels

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the seven 'ro'ei pnei hamelech' of the Megillah, whose names the Gemara connects to korbanos. The Chasam Sofer explains that what happens below happens above, so seven angels with the same names sat in judgment and pleaded for the Jews.

title.en: The 'knowers of the times' and the leap year

summary.en: On the plain level the king's advisers were experts in calculating the calendar, and a calculation about the day Vashti's father was killed is brought. Rashi reads them as the holy angels who busied themselves with the leap year so that Esther would become queen, and the Mashgiach asks what angels have to do with a leap year.

title.en: The moon's flaw and Esther as the moon

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the leap year repairs the moon, which was diminished for lacking a good eye toward the sun. This jealousy is part of creation and runs through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, Kayin and the sale of Yosef; Esther is the moon, and her becoming queen is a repair of its flaw.

title.en: The leap year of the miracle

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that the Sages made the year of the miracle a leap year, so the angels' concern with the leap year was the moon's repair through Esther. He explains that the thirteenth month makes up the days the moon loses against the sun each year, repairing a flaw that came from jealousy and a narrow eye.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai repairs with a good eye

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the students of Rabbi Akiva, who did not honor one another, with the thirteenth middah of Tomer Devorah, seeing another's good. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a gilgul of Shimon who led the sale of Yosef, repaired it with a good eye and love of friends, and like Yosef's twelve years plus one, his twelve years in the cave became thirteen.

title.en: Lag BaOmer and Purim, and the task of the generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Lag BaOmer always falls on the weekday of Purim and explains that they are a pair: Purim's gathering of all the Jews and Rabbi Shimon's 'sheves achim gam yachad' both repair the sale of Yosef and the moon. He closes that the task of this generation is the middah of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, love and peace between friends.

catalogTitle: רשב”י מגלה שיש חן מיוחד בכל יחיד מישראל

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jew, even the lowest, has a hidden virtue and grace before Hashem that no other Jew has, and that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the revealer of secrets, revealed this hidden preciousness of every Jew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rav Tzadok HaKohen's teaching that every Jew has a unique grace before Hashem and a virtue no other Jew has, which makes him a king; this is why Rabbi Shimon says all Jews are sons of kings. The virtue is hidden, like the sod level of the Torah, and Rabbi Shimon, who reveals secrets, reveals it. The students of Rabbi Akiva died for not honoring one another, failing to see this hidden virtue; on Lag Ba'omer it shines more than on other days. He links the four levels of Torah to the four elements, with earth as the lowest Jew, and shows from the shemitah of the land and the Torah's care for the animals that holiness reaches even there. He closes with the Zohar's account of Rabbi Shimon's passing, the name formed from Kiddush, and Rabbi Shimon's special help for the last generation before Moshiach.

en: Every Jew has a special grace before Hashem and a virtue that no other Jew has, and through it he is a king over all Jews.
This virtue is hidden, like the sod level of the Torah, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who reveals secrets, reveals the preciousness of every Jew.

The students of Rabbi Akiva did not honor one another because they did not appreciate the hidden virtue of the other; on Lag Ba'omer the preciousness of each Jew shines out more than on any other day.

The four levels of Torah correspond to the four elements; earth is the lowest level, and the shemitah of the land shows that the holiness of Shabbos reaches down even to it, that is, to the lowest Jew.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the aspect of Shabbos, and his main concern is the last generation, the generation of the footsteps of Moshiach, whom he helps to be raised to the greatest levels.

title.en: Every Jew has a hidden grace

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rav Tzadok HaKohen that every Jew has a unique grace and virtue that makes him a king, the reason Rabbi Shimon says all Jews are sons of kings. The virtue is hidden like the sod of the Torah, and Rabbi Shimon, revealer of secrets, reveals it.

title.en: Rabbi Akiva's students and the lowest element

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Rabbi Akiva's students died for not honoring each other's hidden virtue, and that Lag Ba'omer reveals it. He sets the four levels of Torah against the four elements, with earth as the lowest Jew, and says even earth has a Shabbos and every Jew has a portion in Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: Shabbos reaches down to the earth

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the holiness of Shabbos reaches down to the lowest Jew, brings the Beis Aharon that as Hashem is blessed for all so Rabbi Shimon is for all, and connects Lag Ba'omer with parshas Behar and the shemitah of the land, the amei ha'aretz, and the Zohar's teaching that Rabbi Shimon is the aspect of Shabbos.

title.en: Shemitah, the animals, and 'afra afra'

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that in shemitah the Torah provides even for the animals, an allusion to Jews who seem to have lost their tzelem Elokim, so Lag Ba'omer is a yom tov for the lowly. He ties this to the tribe of Dan, the last camp, and to the students of Rabbi Akiva, and brings the Zohar on Rabbi Shimon's passing, that the earth must not be proud, since he is not consumed by it.

title.en: The name from Kiddush and the last generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls this a comfort for Jews: the holiness of the name formed from the initials of yichud, brachah and kedushah in the Kiddush of Shabbos reaches down to 'the animals and the beasts'. He repeats the Beis Aharon and concludes that Rabbi Shimon's main concern is our generation before Moshiach, ending with a tefilah.

catalogTitle: ממוכן Awakens the Merit of the לחם הפנים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why Memuchan, who is Haman, has a heavenly counterpart pleading with the merit of the lechem hapanim: the bread that stayed warm shows that Hashem's love for even the rejected Jews never grows cold, and that is the miracle of Purim.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Rokeach linking Purim to the lechem hapanim, and the Gemara that the names of Achashverosh's advisers are angels pleading with the merits of the korbanos, the last, Memuchan, with the lechem hapanim, though Memuchan is Haman. He explains that Amalek attacked the cast-outs of Shevet Dan, and that their surplus silver went for the hooks of the pillars, outside the kedushah, which is why Moshe forgot them. The ben ish Mitzri mocked the lechem hapanim, holding like Amalek that Hashem's love for Dan had gone stale. The Mashgiach answers that every Jew has a hidden point that is never a rasha, shown by the two identical goats of Yom Kippur and the Rambam's 'I want'. Haman's ten thousand talents matched only the main half-shekels and ignored the surplus; that surplus neutralized him. Purim is the Yom Tov of the plain Jew, and the Mashgiach ends with this year's three-day Purim in Yerushalayim and a call for tzedakah.

en: According to the Gemara, Memuchan's heavenly counterpart pleads with the merit of the lechem hapanim, and Memuchan is Haman; the shiur sets out to explain the connection.
Amalek attacked the cast-outs of Shevet Dan, who were outside the Clouds of Glory, and Hashem's anger at Amalek is the greatest because they started with His children.
The surplus silver of the half-shekel, given by the Jews who were outside, went for the hooks of the pillars, the one part of the Mishkan outside the kedushah, which is why Moshe Rabbeinu forgot it.
The warm lechem hapanim shows that Hashem's love for every tribe, even Dan, never becomes stale; the ben ish Mitzri who denied the miracle sided with Amalek.
Every Jew has a hidden point, rooted in Avraham Avinu, where he is not a rasha; this is why the two goats of Yom Kippur must be identical.
Haman's ten thousand talents matched only the 600,000 half-shekels, not the surplus of the rejected, and that surplus is what nullified his decree.
Purim is the Yom Tov of the simple Jew, celebrating only that he is a Yid, and in the lowest generations it grows greater.

title.en: Memuchan and the lechem hapanim

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is misunderstood and greater in a way than Yom Kippur. He brings the Rokeach linking Purim to the lechem hapanim and the Gemara that Memuchan's heavenly counterpart pleads with the lechem hapanim, and asks why, since Memuchan is Haman.

title.en: Amalek and the cast-outs of Dan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem's anger at Amalek exceeds that at any other nation because Amalek attacked the idol-worshipping cast-outs of Shevet Dan, who were outside the Clouds of Glory. Hashem's answer is that they are still His children.

title.en: The forgotten silver of the hooks

summary.en: From the reckoning in Parshas Pekudei, the Mashgiach shows that the 600,000 half-shekels went for the sockets and the surplus for the hooks of the pillars, which were outside the kedushah. He reasons that this surplus came from the rejected of Dan, which is why Moshe Rabbeinu forgot it until he was reminded.

title.en: The ben ish Mitzri and the warm bread

summary.en: Following Rashi, the Mashgiach describes how the ben ish Mitzri mocked the lechem hapanim, which stayed warm for nine days, and insisted on a place in Dan's camp. He explains the dispute: the neighbors argued from the twelve separately baked loaves, each dear to Hashem and kept warm, that Dan is not rejected, while he denied the miracle and so took Amalek's position.

title.en: The hidden point in every Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew has an inextinguishable point where he is not a rasha, citing the Ba'al Shem Tov, Reb Tzadok HaKohen on the two identical goats of Yom Kippur and on Yaakov and Esav, and the Rambam on a forced 'I want'. Yom Kippur and Purim both bring this inner will to the surface.

title.en: Haman's silver and the surplus

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Tosafos that Haman's ten thousand talents matched the half-shekels of the 600,000 and asks why Haman did not pay for the surplus. He answers that Haman, like Amalek, discounted the rejected Jews, and their surplus silver came first and nullified his shekalim; Purim is thus the Yom Tov of the plain Jew.

title.en: Haman as the Mitzri, and our generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Yaaros Devash that Haman was a gilgul of the Mitzri whom Moshe killed and Mordechai a gilgul of Moshe, and adds that the ben ish Mitzri therefore shared Haman's view. He returns to the lechem hapanim as proof of the hidden point, and suggests that today's generation are gilgulim of Shevet Dan.

title.en: The Yom Tov of the rejected

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is the Yom Tov of the rejected, whose joy is simply being a Yid, as Mordechai would not bow because he was a Yid. He contrasts milah, the point of the Jew, with tefillin, the mitzvos, says Purim has both, and that each Purim grows greater as the generations fall lower.

title.en: Three-day Purim and a call for tzedakah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes this year's three-day Purim in Yerushalayim, which Shabbos magnifies, and says it reaches all of Klal Yisrael at a time of danger with no natural solution. He closes by urging the listeners to rest, hear every word of the Megillah, and give more tzedakah than they can, since the miracle came through the extra silver.

catalogTitle: שיהיו דברי תורה חדשים עליך; ביאתם לסיני בתשובה

oneLiner.en: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Mashgiach teaches that the Torah is given anew every year, and that the arrival at Sinai, made in unity and teshuvah, is a time to take on new resolutions whose acceptance itself sustains the world.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by explaining why the people gather in the days before Shavuos: sitting together as one man with one heart is a goal in itself, and the Gemara shows that avodah needs a stir of many people. Following the Avodas Yisroel, he studies the verses of Bachodesh hashlishi day by day. Rashi's words 'that the words of Torah be new to you as if given today' answer the Magen Avraham's question about 'the day of the giving of our Torah': it is given anew each year. Rosh Chodesh is the renewal of the moon, a time to take on new kabbalos, and from the Simchas HaRegel and the Gemara in Shabbos he shows how precious acceptance itself is. Leaving Rephidim means shaking off weakness in Torah with teshuvah. He speaks of unity, facing the 'east', the dangers facing Jews and the apathy of the world, and ends that each Jew's added acceptance can tip the whole world.

en: Sitting together as one man with one heart before Shavuos is a goal in itself, and it is also the setting for words of chizuk.
The Torah is given anew every Shavuos, so the words of Torah must feel new each day, as if given today.
Rosh Chodesh, the renewal of the moon, renews the spiritual growth in a Jew's soul and is a time to take on new kabbalos.
Accepting the mitzvos is itself precious to Hashem; the world waited not for the giving of the Torah but for the Jews' acceptance of it.
Leaving Rephidim, read as weakness in Torah, means shaking off that weakness with teshuvah and strengthening oneself in Torah.
A Jew should face 'east', toward the one point of glorifying Hashem and toward the future, not back at lost days.
Since the world's existence hangs on accepting the Torah, each Jew's added acceptance before Shavuos can tip the whole world to merit.

title.en: Why gather before Shavuos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that sitting together as one man with one heart is a goal in itself, brings the Avodas Yisroel's custom of learning the verses of Bachodesh hashlishi each day from Rosh Chodesh, and cites the Gemara that the Temple service was arranged with several lotteries so there would be a stir of people.

title.en: Torah new each day; Rosh Chodesh renewal

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers the Magen Avraham's question on 'the day of the giving of our Torah' by explaining that the Torah is given anew every year, reads Rashi's 'that the words of Torah be new to you', and explains that the Jews arrived at Sinai on Rosh Chodesh because the renewal of the moon renews a Jew's soul and is the time for new kabbalos, even though all beginnings are hard.

title.en: The power of kabbalah

summary.en: From the Simchas HaRegel, citing Rabbi Gedalia Chayun on a Midrash, the Mashgiach explains that every mitzvah a convert does is compounded by the mitzvah of her acceptance; the Gemara's 'you captured My heart with one of your eyes' shows that acceptance alone is dear to Hashem, and the world waited for the Jews' acceptance of the Torah.

title.en: Leaving Rephidim with teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Rosh Chodesh is when the Jews accepted upon themselves with teshuvah, urges taking on one middah to work on, reads Rephidim as weakness in Torah, and brings Rashi that their arrival at Sinai and their departure from Rephidim were both with teshuvah.

title.en: One heart, facing east

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Sinai's unity with the strife elsewhere, ties Sivan's sign of twins to unity, and explains Rashi's 'wherever it says neged, it means facing east' as being turned toward the one point of glorifying Hashem and toward the future; he ends with the Gemara that the earth feared until the Jews accepted the Torah.

title.en: The danger and the world's apathy

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the danger facing Jews in Eretz Yisroel and the growing hatred elsewhere, says the world suffers from apathy and distraction, and tells how his father-in-law once rebuked a Vienna community meeting busy with honor while Hitler grew strong; the only counsel is accepting Torah and mitzvos and davening for Klal Yisroel.

title.en: Each Jew can tip the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the world's existence hung on the acceptance of the Torah, brings the Gemara that one person can tip the whole world to merit, asks each one to take on a little more learning and coming earlier to davening, and closes with Rashi that Moshe's ascents were early in the morning, a blessing and a l'chaim.

catalogTitle: ויחן שם ישראל - חשיבות דיבוק חברים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Jews camped before Sinai 'as one man with one heart', and that this unity among friends is the general principle of the Torah and the preparation for receiving it; in the second part he explains why Shavuos, the fiftieth day, stands above time and counting.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with 'bachodesh hashlishi... bayom hazeh' and Rashi's reading that it was Rosh Chodesh, a new beginning tied to Matan Torah. Rashi compares leaving Refidim to arriving at Sinai, both in teshuvah. The Mashgiach explains that Refidim was a place of separation, which let Amalek in, and the repair was 'vayichan', camping as one man with one heart. This is why the Haggadah praises nearing Sinai even without the Torah: love of one's fellow is the klal of the Torah, and on that day nothing was said, yet they became one. He brings the Kobriner and the Lechovitcher and urges friends to sit together. After a long gap, he asks why Shavuos is the day of the giving of the Torah and explains that the fiftieth day is above counting, like the Levi'im, Aharon and Moshe Rabbeinu, and that Moshe, the 'shofar' of Klal Yisrael, brings the festivals each year.

en: Rosh Chodesh Sivan, when the Jews camped before Sinai as one man with one heart, is a day whose whole theme is unity among Jews.
Refidim was a place of separation among Jews, which gave Amalek his power; the teshuvah on leaving it was their unity.
Coming close to Sinai in unity is the general principle of the Torah, 'love your fellow as yourself', while the giving of the Torah brought its details.
In a lowly generation little is demanded, and a small effort toward unity among friends is precious in heaven and can bring great things.
The fiftieth day is above counting and above time, which is why it is not counted, like the Levi'im, Aharon and Moshe Rabbeinu who stand above number.
Moshe Rabbeinu, the 'shofar' of Klal Yisrael, could rule over time, and he brings the power of Matan Torah to every Jewish shul each Shavuos.

title.en: Untranscribed opening

summary.en: About three minutes at the start where the ASR caught only a few words.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh Sivan and leaving Refidim

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'bachodesh hashlishi... bayom hazeh' with Rashi that it was Rosh Chodesh, and explains that a new month, a new beginning, is tied to Matan Torah. He then brings Rashi that their leaving Refidim was compared to their arrival at Sinai: both in teshuvah.

title.en: 'Vayichan': as one man with one heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi on 'vayichan sham Yisrael', that they camped as one man with one heart, and explains that Refidim was a place of separation that let Amalek in, so their teshuvah was unity. He adds that two Jews together form Hashem's Name, and that today's theme is that Jews should sit together and love one another.

title.en: Nearing Sinai: the klal of the Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks what virtue there is in coming close to Sinai without receiving the Torah, as the Haggadah says, and answers that the unity of that day is 'love your fellow as yourself', Rabbi Akiva's great principle of the Torah. He brings the practice of sitting together in friendship from Beis Aharon and the Gemara that on Rosh Chodesh nothing was said to them.

title.en: One family; naaseh v'nishma as one

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rav Moshe of Kobrin that when Jews sit together as one family they are not excluded from the klal, and explains that naaseh v'nishma was so great because it was said as one. He contrasts the decline of the generations with the greater virtue of today, when little is demanded and a small effort can merit great things.

title.en: Greater light in the darkness; no complaints against friends

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that because the darkness is greater, Hashem lights greater lamps, as seen in the revelations from Rashbi, the Arizal and the Ba'al Shem Tov, and the small piece one can give is precious in heaven. He brings the Lechovitcher that a punishment is to be sent complaints against one's Rebbe and then against one's friends, and says one must bear a friend's faults, since every Jew is a part of G-d above, as the preparation for receiving the Torah.

title.en: Long untranscribed gap

summary.en: Almost fourteen minutes where the ASR caught only one short line.

title.en: Why Shavuos is 'the time of the giving of the Torah'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the question that the Torah was given on the fifty-first day of the Omer, on Shabbos, so how is Shavuos called the day of the giving of the Torah, and the Chok Yaakov's discussion of it. He brings that whenever the parsha of Matan Torah is read, it is as if one stands before Sinai receiving the Torah.

title.en: The fiftieth day and the uncounted Levi'im

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Rashi on the dots over Aharon's name in the count of the Levi'im, and the Chok Yaakov that Shavuos depends on the fiftieth day of the count, not the date. The fiftieth day is above place, time and number, where 'one' is not the smallest number but the only one, like the Levi'im who were not counted with the camps because they stand above counting.

title.en: Three levels of one miracle

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Mishnah of ten miracles in the Beis Hamikdash does not count that the place of the Aron took no space, and answers that in the Kodesh HaKodashim heaven's nature rules, so it is no miracle, like fish in the sea. Bowing with room in the Azarah was a visible miracle on Yom Tov, and finding lodging in Yerushalayim a hidden one: the same miracle at three levels.

title.en: Aharon, Moshe and the fiftieth gate

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that among the uncounted there are levels: the Levi'im, then Aharon, of whom not even the firstborn part was counted, and Moshe Rabbeinu, the fiftieth gate, connected with Rabbi Akiva's 'great principle'. He brings that the Torah is above time, the dispute whether it was given on the sixth or seventh of Sivan, and that the sixth of Sivan was set from creation.

title.en: Moshe Rabbeinu, the shofar who brings the festivals

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Moshe Rabbeinu, the shofar of Klal Yisrael, stood above time and added a day, as later the heads of Beis Din could set the months, while today the calendar is fixed on the sixth of Sivan. 'Vayedaber Moshe es mo'adei Hashem' means Moshe brings the festivals to the Jews, so every Shavuos he comes to every shul where the parsha is read, and it is truly 'bayom hazeh'.

title.en: Counting the last sefirah together

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the last count of sefirah includes all the days, speaks of 'sur mera va'aseh tov' as the work of sefirah, and asks that everyone come together to daven and count sefirah together.

catalogTitle: כל יהודי הוא מיוחס - בן להקב”ה. נפלאותך ומחשבותיך אלינו - לבל ידח ממנו נדח

oneLiner.en: On Yom HaMeyuchas the Mashgiach teaches that every Jew is a meyuchas, a son of the King, and that Hashem's thoughts are all directed at bringing every Jewish soul, even the most distant, to its tikkun, as seen in the line of David and in Menashe's halachah of where to cut the bread.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens on Yom HaMeyuchas, the second of Sivan: the yetzer hara's greatest trick is making a Jew forget he is a king's son. Through the pesukim of the day he shows how Hashem first lifted the Jews to Yerushalayim for the Korban Pesach and then returned them, because a king's son must earn what is his by right. He reads 've'ata' as a call to do teshuvah now rather than wait for another gilgul. From 'nifle'osecha u'machshevosecha eleinu' he explains that every soul is a letter in Hashem's Sefer Torah, so none may be lost; the hidden, puzzling paths of Beis David, through Tamar, Ruth and yibum, are part of this plan. Boaz's hint that Menashe would come from Ruth leads to the Gemara of Rav Ashi learning from Menashe where to break bread. Stories of Belz show that a brachah repairs souls in food, and the crust baked first is Hashem's sign of which piece reaches its tikkun first.

en: The Mashgiach says the yetzer hara's greatest scheme is to make a Jew forget that he is a king's son, a meyuchas, with virtues he did not earn himself.
Hashem showed the Jews their destination by bringing them to Yerushalayim for the Korban Pesach, but brought them back because a king's son must work through the process himself.
'Ve'ata' means now: the Mashgiach asks why wait for a later time or another gilgul to do teshuvah and accept the Torah.
All of Hashem's thoughts are concentrated on the Jewish people's tikkun; every soul is a letter in His Sefer Torah, so a soul that has not completed itself must return until it does.
Malchus Beis David comes into the world through hidden and puzzling paths, such as Tamar, Ruth and yibum, because it is built from the tikkun of souls that were pushed away.
Menashe, whom Boaz called the 'vinegar' that would come from Ruth, became the teacher of all Israel through the halachah of where to break bread.
Food holds sparks and souls awaiting their tikkun, and a brachah said with kavanah repairs them.

title.en: Every Jew a meyuchas, a king's son

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that on this day every Jew should feel he is a meyuchas, and that the yetzer hara's chief trick is making him forget he is a king's son. He brings the Avodas Yisrael's custom of learning the pesukim of each day from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, Rashi's comparison of the departure from Refidim to the arrival at Sinai, and the pesukim of the second of Sivan.

title.en: Brought to Yerushalayim and brought back

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the words Hashem spoke to Moshe on this day are said again every year and the soul hears them. On 'va'avi eschem elai' he brings Targum Yonasan that the Jews were carried to Yerushalayim for the Korban Pesach and returned, and asks why; he answers that a Jew has his destination in potential but must reach it in actual through his own work, like a king's son.

title.en: Onkelos, Ramban and 've'ata'

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Onkelos, who renders 'elai' as being brought near to Hashem's service out of respect, with the Ramban, who reads it as Hashem dwelling together with the Jews like a father with a child. He then reads 've'ata' as a call to do teshuvah now, and begins explaining 'segulah' as a hidden treasure.

title.en: A hidden treasure and 'na'aseh' every year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Jews' virtues are hidden like a king's treasure that only Hashem understands, bringing a Rebbe's reading of Haman's words. He describes how the people answered together without waiting for the elders, and says the Torah is eternal, so every year on this day every Jewish soul again cries out 'kol asher diber Hashem na'aseh'.

title.en: Why wait for another gilgul?

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to 've'ata' and brings a parable from Lechovitch about a man who keeps returning to the world only to act foolishly again. From 'nifle'osecha u'machshevosecha eleinu' he explains that all of Hashem's thoughts are directed at the tikkun of the Jews, and that a soul missing a mitzvah must return in another gilgul to complete itself, since Hashem's Torah is whole.

title.en: Every soul a letter; Naomi gathers the sparks

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Jewish soul is part of one of the letters of the Torah, so a missing soul would invalidate the Sefer Torah. He turns to Megillas Rus: Elimelech went to Moav, where sparks of kedushah were hidden from which David and Moshiach must come, and Naomi, representing the Shechinah, went along to gather them. He connects this to the Rambam's sign of Moshiach, gathering the dispersed of Israel.

title.en: Beis David built through yibum

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Shavuos is the time of gathering, when the Jews camped 'as one man with one heart', and that Moshiach is Hashem's instrument to gather and repair all Jews. He shows that Malchus Beis David repeatedly came through yibum, with Yehudah and Tamar and with Boaz and Ruth, because yibum is the tikkun of a soul that was pushed away.

title.en: Boaz's hint: Menashe the 'vinegar'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that Boaz's words to Ruth about dipping her bread in vinegar hinted that Menashe, whose deeds were sour, would descend from her. He describes Menashe, son of the tzaddik Chizkiyahu, who placed an idol in the Heichal, and the dispute whether he has a share in the World to Come, and introduces the Gemara of Rav Ashi.

title.en: Menashe teaches Rav Ashi where to cut

summary.en: The Mashgiach retells the Gemara in Sanhedrin: Menashe came to Rav Ashi in a dream and taught him to break bread from the place baked first, and this halachah is codified for all generations. So every Jew who says hamotzi follows Menashe, his rebbe; Boaz was in fact comforting Ruth, and the Mashgiach asks why this halachah specifically came through Menashe, noting that a person's Torah is his very soul.

title.en: The kugel on the floor and the glass of brandy

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells that at Reb Sholom of Belz's tish a piece of kugel fell to the floor and he had it picked up and eaten, and explains that eating is not a mere biological function: souls and sparks in food are rectified by a proper brachah. He tells of a Jew who drank brandy without a brachah, and a tzaddik who revealed that his father's soul had been in the drink awaiting its tikkun.

title.en: The prayers of a wheat kernel

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Reb Sholom of Belz's explanation: a kernel of wheat prayed at every stage, growing, harvest, grinding, baking, to reach its tikkun, until it became challah and then Shabbos kugel at the tzaddik's tish; letting it fall would waste all those prayers. The Mashgiach concludes that a Jew should eat with thought and make a brachah with kavanah, and that this repairs the souls hidden in the food.

title.en: The melachos of bread and the crust baked first

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the melachos of bread in the Gemara Shabbos are stages of the tikkun that came after Adam's sin, ending with baking. He asks why Rav Ashi did not know where to break bread and why not from the tastiest part, and answers that the place baked first is a sign of Hashem's plan that this piece reach its tikkun first; one must look into Hashem's intention in all of Torah and mitzvos.

title.en: Hashem's intention, and Menashe's teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts selling chametz, which serves Hashem's intention that a Jew not own chametz, with selling Eretz Yisrael for Shemitah, which goes against it. Returning to the bread, he says Beis David is a seed meant to repair the world, and retells the Gemara of Menashe's teshuvah, which Hashem accepted out of chesed against the angels' claims; Menashe is a sample of the wondrous ways of David's line, which is why his soul brought the halachah of hamotzi.

catalogTitle: מרדכי and אסתר Rectified the חטא עץ הדעת

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the root of Adam's sin, of the Golden Calf and of the error at Achashverosh's feast was not waiting, that Mordechai came to repair it, and that on Purim and in Parshas Parah Hashem reaches even the Jews who stand outside.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi's account of the Golden Calf: the people counted Moshe's forty days from the day he went up, and erred. Why could they not apply the rule that part of a day counts as a whole? Through the Bnei Yissaschar's teaching that a mikveh's forty se'ah hold 960 lugin, and that Matan Torah is a rebirth like a mikveh, he shows that 960 full hours were needed. Every mistake has a root: the people did not wait, just as Adam did not wait for Shabbos to make Kiddush from the Tree of Knowledge. The same error recurred when the Jews miscounted the seventy years and went to Achashverosh's feast, while Mordechai warned them to wait. The Mashgiach applies this to waiting for Moshiach today. He then discusses the five final letters, Haman's shekalim, the forgotten hooks of the pillars, the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan, Tehillim 34, and Parshas Parah as a salvation reaching those who are outside.

en: Matan Torah was a rebirth like immersion in a mikveh, so it required forty complete days of 24 hours, 960 hours matching the 960 lugin of a mikveh; the rule that part of a day counts as a whole does not apply.
The root of the error at the Golden Calf, and of Adam's sin before it, was not waiting: Adam should have waited for Shabbos to make Kiddush over the juice of the Tree of Knowledge.

The Jews who went to Achashverosh's feast repeated the same mistake: they thought the seventy years had passed without redemption, while Mordechai warned them to wait, making him a repair of Adam's sin.
The Mashgiach says the task of our generation is to wait for Moshiach and not to think that the redemption has already come.
The extra 1775 shekalim, which became the hooks of the pillars, correspond to the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan who stood outside the camp, and Haman's money did not counter their merit.
At the root of every Jewish soul, called Kol Yisrael, no sin can reach, and from there Hashem shows favor even to those who do not deserve it, as on Purim.
Parshas Parah, read after Purim, continues Purim: the red heifer is burned outside the camp and brings salvation to those who are outside.

title.en: Forty full days: Matan Torah as a mikveh

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks, from Rashi on the Golden Calf, why part of the first day could not count for Moshe's forty days. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar that a mikveh's forty se'ah are 960 lugin, the measure in which even a creature is nullified, so that the 960 hours of Elul to Yom Kippur are a mikveh, and applies this to Matan Torah, which needed 960 full hours.

title.en: The root of the mistake: not waiting

summary.en: The Mashgiach says every mistake has a root: the people did not wait one more day, just as Adam did not wait for Shabbos to make Kiddush from the Tree of Knowledge. Had they waited, Matan Torah would have brought the perfected world. He tells of the Malbim describing to the maskilim how a Jew must wait before he may eat, and concludes that the whole Torah is built on waiting.

title.en: Achashverosh's feast and Mordechai's repair

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the seventy years were miscalculated, and explains that the Jews went to Achashverosh's feast because they thought the redemption would no longer come, while Mordechai warned them to wait. Mordechai was thus a repair of Adam's sin, since the Tree of Knowledge mixed good and evil and waiting for Shabbos would have left only its good.

title.en: Our task now: waiting for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the lesson: the repair of the sin is to wait for Moshiach. Though the signs in the Gemara fit this generation, one must not think the redemption has come; he calls the State of Israel a mixture of good and evil, and brings the navi's words about waiting for Hashem who hides His face.

title.en: The five final letters: din and geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings, from the Bnei Yissaschar in the name of the Arizal, that the five final letters are letters of din, the 280 judgments, and also, according to the Midrash, letters of redemption, each tied to a geulah from Avraham to the final one. He brings the passuk in Yeshayahu about awaiting the tzaddik and shows the five letters in Haman, Zeresh and his wise men.

title.en: Haman's shekalim and the forgotten Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Haman's ten thousand kikar matched the half-shekel of the 600,000, but not the extra 1775 shekalim that Moshe forgot and that became the hooks of the pillars. These correspond to the letters at the very end of the Torah and to the rejected Jews of the tribe of Dan, whom the cloud did not protect and Amalek attacked; Haman gave nothing against them, and they brought the salvation.

title.en: Tehillim 34 and the tribe of Dan

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that Tehillim 34, whose verse forms the letter combination of Dan's month, follows the whole aleph-beis and adds one last verse outside it, about Hashem redeeming His servants; this verse belongs to Dan's rejected ones and equals in gematria the hooks of the pillars. The whole aleph-beis with the five final letters totals 1775, the forgotten shekalim, showing they are included in Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Kol Yisrael: the root no sin reaches

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem cares so much for the rejected of Dan, and answers from Parshas Ki Sisa, read near Purim: Hashem shows favor even to those who do not deserve it, looking to the root of the Jewish soul. He brings the Yismach Moshe on the 'island' of Kol Yisrael that no sin can blemish and the Rambam that every Jew inwardly wants Hashem's will, and ties this to the salvation of Purim and to 'ad delo yada'.

title.en: Parshas Parah: salvation outside the camp

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parshas Parah after Purim continues Purim and sweetens the 280 judgments. He brings the Tanya's question why the red heifer atones more than a chatas, and adds that the parah is done outside the camp, bringing salvation to those outside, like the last letters of the Torah. He closes with a brachah to be purified for Pesach.

catalogTitle: ביאור עמוק על מגילת רות. השכינה - נעמי' באה אל מואב להוציא משם ניצוץ משיח - זה רות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Megillas Rus as the story of how the spark of Moshiach is drawn out of Moav in a time like ikvesa d'Meshicha, and how Rus, who held to the old tradition and accepted the Torah when it was hard, is the model for accepting the Torah on Shavuos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Gemara that Rus is so named because David, who came from her, sated Hashem with songs even in hard times. He brings the Gemara that Machlon and Kilyon despaired of the redemption, and the mekubalim's teaching on gilgulim, and explains that the Shechinah, Naomi, went down to Moav to draw out the holy soul of Rus. He then asks why the megillah opens with the days when the judges were judged, and why Chazal read immodesty into its verses. Through the Gemara's signs of ikvesa d'Meshicha, he explains that before Moshiach the lower forces of evil must be kept busy, like Iyov at the Sea, so chutzpah and disorder accompany the birth of Moshiach. Rus, who converted in hard times and clung to her mother-in-law's way, brought Moshiach. He closes with Malachi, Shavuos, and a call to prepare for kabbalas haTorah.

en: Rus is named for David, who came from her and could sing to Hashem even on a day of trouble, knowing that hard times are also from Hashem and good times will return.
Naomi represents the Shechinah, who went down into Moav, the territory of the sitra achra, to draw out the spark of Moshiach, Rus, and this is why there had to be a famine and Elimelech had to leave.
Before Moshiach, the lower forces of evil, which oppose Hashem's plan, must be kept busy with something, like a bone thrown to a dog, and this is the source of the chaos of ikvesa d'Meshicha.
The megillah opens with the generation that judged its judges because the signs of ikvesa d'Meshicha, chutzpah, famine and immodesty, accompany the birth of the spark of David and Moshiach.
Rus converted when it was hard to be a Jew, giving up royalty, and her reward was to live to see Shlomo's kingship, a time when converts are not accepted.
The disorder of the generation does not bring Moshiach; it is only a symptom. Rus brought Moshiach by holding to her mother-in-law's old way, the opposite of Orpah who turned her back.
Shavuos, when the Torah is received, is a time of power to leave the exile, and the Mashgiach calls for preparing for kabbalas haTorah in the remaining days.

converts in the days of Shlomo

title.en: Why she is called Rus

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Rus is named for David, who sated Hashem with songs. He explains that Rus accepted poverty and disgrace for the Torah, and that David could sing even on a day of trouble because he knew hard times are also from Hashem.

title.en: Gilgulim, Shavuos and the Shechinah in Moav

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Machlon and Kilyon despaired of the redemption, and the mekubalim's teaching that the people of the megillah were gilgulim come to rectify earlier deeds. He explains that the Torah must be kept whole, so a soul returns to complete it, and that the Shechinah, Naomi, went down to Moav to draw out the holy soul of Rus.

title.en: The generation that judged its judges

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the chaos of the days when the judges were judged and asks: the opening words of a megillah usually set its background, yet Megillas Rus says nothing further about this situation, speaking only of Rus, Boaz and David's lineage.

title.en: Chazal read immodesty into the megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that Boaz slept at the edge of the grain pile to guard it from being used for immorality, and that he asked about Rus because she did not behave like the other girls with the reapers. He contrasts this with the Gemara where Rabbi Yochanan refuses to suspect the maidens who spoke at length to Shaul, and asks why Chazal here read immodesty into the verses.

title.en: The signs of ikvesa d'Meshicha

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the Gemara's description of the time before Moshiach: chutzpah, hunger, scorn for Torah scholars and the fearful of sin, the young shaming the old, and nothing to lean on but our Father in Heaven. He explains the erev rav as those who act for themselves and not for Heaven, and asks why the world must break down before Moshiach instead of improving step by step.

title.en: Keeping the lower forces of evil busy

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the forces of evil have layers: the higher ones know Hashem and do His will, but the lowest do not want His plan fulfilled. He brings the Midrash that at Kerias Yam Suf the Satan accused Yisrael and Hashem sent him to Iyov, and concludes that before Moshiach Hashem gives the Satan something to occupy him, like a bone thrown to a dog so it will not disturb the feast.

title.en: The megillah's goal is David and Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the whole purpose of Megillas Rus is its last verse, the birth of David, so its theme is the coming of Moshiach. When the Shechinah goes into Moav to rescue the spark of David and Moshiach, the sitra achra must be given something, and so the time of the Judges bears the signs of ikvesa d'Meshicha, including the hunger and Elimelech's refusal to give charity.

title.en: Chutzpah as the camouflage of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers his question: since the megillah does not state the signs openly, Chazal find them by remez and derash in Boaz's lying at the edge of the pile and in the girls with the reapers. Generations later, in David's time, there was no such immodesty, so Rabbi Yochanan would not suspect the maidens. The very first point of Moshiach, through Lot's daughter who named her son Moav, also began with chutzpah, which covers the coming of Moshiach and keeps the forces of evil busy.

title.en: Rus's complete reward and 'stay the night'

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Boaz's blessing that Rus's reward will be complete: the Gemara says converts are not accepted in the days of Moshiach or Shlomo, and the Rambam explains that a convert is accepted when being a Jew is hard. Rus gave up royalty to convert in hard times, so her reward was to see Shlomo's glory. He then brings Chazal on 'stay the night': through the night of exile, if good people do not redeem, Hashem Himself will.

title.en: From Malachi to Rus

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Rus begins right after Malachi, the last prophet, who closes with 'remember the Torah of Moshe' and the promise of Eliyahu, who will turn the hearts of fathers to sons. Until Eliyahu comes, the generations are torn apart, which is the state of 'the days when the judges were judged'; this is a sign Moshiach is coming, a reason to hope and not to despair like Machlon and Kilyon.

title.en: How Rus brought Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach connects Rus to Shavuos, when David was born and when, according to the Zohar, there is power to leave the exile through the Torah. The immodest of that generation were only symptoms of Moshiach, like a swallow before spring; Rus, unlike Orpah, held to her mother-in-law's old ways and so brought Moshiach. He says every Jew must learn from her to accept the Torah even when the whole world is against it, like Avraham ha'Ivri, and that the Torah was given in the desert.

title.en: 'And now': preparing for kabbalas haTorah

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'and now, if you will listen' with Rashi that all beginnings are hard: now it is hard, but later it will be sweet, and those who held out in exile like Rus will see the kingdom. He brings the Gemara that with Torah a full vessel holds more, and calls for using the remaining days of hagbalah to prepare and take on kabbalos for kabbalas haTorah.

catalogTitle: ביאור אקדמות - מנהג ישראל' עיקר מהות של שבועות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the piyut Akdamus line by line, showing how the custom of saying it before the Shavuos Torah reading expresses the praise of Hashem, the song of the angels and the unique song of the Jewish people, and the reward awaiting them.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by stressing that although saying Akdamus is only a custom, a custom of the Jewish people carries the weight of Torah, and great tzaddikim were chosen to recite it. Following the piyut, he explains why one opens by asking permission, why the world is called olam (hidden), and why the fiftieth day is beyond counting. He describes the countless angels created anew each morning, each taking permission from the other, and draws a lesson of unity. The highest song, he says, is the silent one, and every Jew has his own point of knowledge of Hashem, hidden in his heart, illustrated by the story of the treasure under the bridge. Angels sing once in their lives; Jews may sing at every moment, in light and in darkness, like a soldier always on duty. He then explains toil in Torah, the nations' question 'what is your beloved', and the Jews' answer: the light of Moshiach, Olam Haba and the feast of the tzaddikim.

en: Saying Akdamus is only a custom, but a custom of the Jewish people carries the weight of Torah and of what was given at Sinai.
Every angel and every Jew is only one part of a great choir; each takes permission from the other, and only together does the song before Hashem become complete.
The highest song is the silent one: what a person cannot put into words, his private knowledge of Hashem according to his own measure.
The treasure of fear of Heaven lies in every Jew's heart; one need not leap to the heavens to find Hashem but only open the heart.
An angel may sing only once in its lifetime, while a Jew can sing to Hashem at every moment, morning and night, and in times of darkness as well.
Torah acquired through toil becomes a person's own, unlike Torah that came to him without effort.
The nations mock the Jews and invite them to assimilate; the Jews answer that in the days of Moshiach and in Olam Haba their greatness will be revealed.
