the Jewish people and the nations
Olam Haba and the feast of the tzaddikim

title.en: Akdamus: a custom with the weight of Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that saying Akdamus is not a Torah obligation but a custom, and that a custom of the Jewish people is Torah, as if given at Sinai. He describes the great holiness the tzaddikim saw in Akdamus and brings the Sefer Charedim that singing praise to Hashem is part of loving Him.

title.en: Asking permission and the hidden world

summary.en: Explaining the opening lines, the Mashgiach says one asks permission before speaking praise, as a chazzan must, and begins with only a few words. He explains that olam comes from 'hidden', that the fiftieth day is beyond counting, and that even if the heavens were parchment and the seas ink, Hashem's greatness could not be written.

title.en: The angels' song and the unity it teaches

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Hashem created the worlds without effort, the countless angels created anew each morning, and the serafim who wait for permission and take it from one another. From this he teaches that every Jew must know he is one part of a great choir, and why the students of the Ba'al Shem Tov laid such weight on friendship.

title.en: The silent song and each Jew's own knowledge

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the angels' Kedushah with a roar like great waters, then explains the line about praise in a whisper: the highest song is the silent one, like the secrets of the Torah that cannot be conveyed to another. Every Jew knows Hashem according to his own measure, as in 'noda bashe'arim ba'alah', and has a root in Dovid HaMelech's Tehillim.

title.en: Where is His place? The treasure under the bridge

summary.en: The Mashgiach lays out levels of praise, from the mouth to the lips to the innermost parts, as in 'Barchi nafshi'. He explains that one who has not yet arrived thinks Hashem is far away, but the Torah is 'not in heaven', and tells the story of the man who traveled to Hamburg for a treasure that lay under his own oven: the treasure of fear of Heaven is in every Jew's heart.

title.en: An angel sings once; a Jew every moment

summary.en: Explaining the lines on the angels' ordered Kedushah, the Mashgiach says a new angel may sing only once in its whole existence, while Hashem's beloved portion, Yisrael, praises Him at fixed times morning and evening. He asks why one should not use the chance the angels long for, to sing to Hashem at every moment.

title.en: A whole life as a song, morning and night

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rambam that one comes to love of Hashem by contemplating His creation, and says this is most fitting at sunrise and sunset, when the whole creation sings. A person's whole life is a song, each with his own kind of niggun, and Yisrael praise Hashem in the morning and at night.

title.en: Serving in darkness: the soldier on duty

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that man was created with 'ratzo vashov', rising and falling, and that even the greatest tzaddikim had dark periods; then too one must serve Hashem. He tells of a soldier who left his post to swim and was caught by the king's inspection, and says a Jew is a soldier who must always be ready, in the morning and in the dark.

title.en: Toil in Torah and the crown of prayer

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem desires that Yisrael toil in Torah: Torah learned with toil is a person's own acquisition, unlike the Torah a child is taught before birth. When a Jew toils in Torah his prayer is accepted, and each accepted prayer becomes a jewel set in Hashem's crown, opposite His tefillin.

title.en: The Jews' mission and the waves of the nations

summary.en: Turning to Hashem's tefillin, the Mashgiach speaks of the greatness of Yisrael and their task to spread emunah among the nations, bringing the Rambam at the end of Hilchos Melachim. He then describes the nations coming at the Jews like waves crashing against grains of sand, asking why they sit in the beis medrash instead of joining their society.

title.en: 'What is your beloved?' and the Jews' answer

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that Akdamus here draws on the verse 'What is your beloved more than another, O fairest among women', and describes the nations' temptation to leave Yiddishkeit for honor and comfort. The Jews answer that the nations cannot yet understand, but when Moshiach comes the great light will show what Yisrael always had, even in exile.

title.en: The nations' shame and an endless joy

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that when Moshiach comes the nations will admit that what they thought were great things were nothing, and Hashem will repay His enemies. He contrasts worldly pleasure, which ends once one is full, with the joy Hashem will give, which never becomes stale and is always renewed.

title.en: Olam Haba that no eye has seen

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that all the prophets prophesied only about the days of Moshiach, but of Olam Haba 'no eye has seen'. He explains with a rule that the holier a thing is, the more easily it is affected, and so Olam Haba is so holy that it was hidden even from the prophets.

title.en: The battle of the Shor HaBar and the Leviasan

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes, from the Midrashim, the great contest between the Shor HaBar and the Leviasan that the tzaddikim will see, and says only those who kept away from the nations' spectacles and sat over the Gemara will merit to watch it. He adds a hint that this contest reflects the struggle between the good and the evil inclination, which Hashem Himself will end.

title.en: The feast of the tzaddikim and the Torah reading

summary.en: The Mashgiach finishes the description of the great feast Hashem will prepare for the tzaddikim, with the wine that has been kept for them. He then turns to the congregation about to hear the Aseres HaDibros, as the tzaddikim heard them at Sinai, and blesses them to merit the company of the tzaddikim.

catalogTitle: מהר"ל - תורה היא מוכרח ולמעלה מן הזמן' קרבן שתי הלחם

oneLiner.en: Building on the Maharal, the Mashgiach explains that Matan Torah is above time, which is why the fiftieth day is not counted and why the Shavuos offering of the two loaves is chametz, and he describes the Sefirah work of 'kedoshim tihyu' that prepares a person for it.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash on 'to everything there is a season': Adam's entry into and exit from Gan Eden, the Flood, and Avraham's milah all came at times fixed from Creation, since nothing in a world built with such harmony is chance. For Matan Torah, however, the verse says 'eis', not 'zman', because an 'eis' is a dimensionless point, and the Torah is above time. Therefore the fiftieth day is not counted, like Yovel and Yom Kippur. Following the Maharal, the Shavuos offering is chametz: chametz is the yetzer hara, and through the Torah it is refined and can serve Hashem. Sefirah refines the seven middos, counting downward from chesed because Shavuos brings Heaven down. The Mashgiach then develops 'kedoshim tihyu' as command and promise, with a story of the Rozvadover, a story of the Stoliner Rebbe's chesed, and practical guidance on growing in holiness step by step.

en: Every major event in history, including sins and their consequences, came at a time fixed in Hashem's plan from Creation; nothing happens by chance.
Matan Torah is called an 'eis', a point that has no extension, because the Torah is above time; for this reason the fiftieth day is not counted in Sefirah.
The Shavuos offering of the two loaves is chametz because through the Torah the yetzer hara, symbolized by chametz, is refined and can be used to serve Hashem.
Sefirah is the work of refining the seven middos, and it counts from chesed down to malchus because Shavuos is about bringing Heaven down to the world.
'Kedoshim tihyu' is both a command and a promise: if a person sanctifies himself a little, Hashem, who is holy, sanctifies him much more.
On Pesach the Jews were lifted up from Above with a strong hand, but the next day it is lost, and through Sefirah a person must reach Shavuos through his own work.
Holiness is built gradually: a person needs some gratification, and should give up a little at a time rather than all at once.

candidateTopics: Sefiras HaOmer and the seven middos

title.en: A set time for every great event

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash on 'to everything there is a season': Adam's entry into and exit from Gan Eden, the Flood, and Avraham's milah each had a fixed time. He explains from the harmony of creation that nothing is chance, and that even a sin and its consequence were prepared in advance.

title.en: 'Eis' and 'zman': the Torah above time

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the Midrash uses 'eis' for Matan Torah: 'zman' is a stretch of time, while 'eis' is a point with no dimension. Matan Torah is above time, like the fiftieth day beyond seven times seven, which is why it is not counted, and he compares it to Yovel and Yom Kippur.

title.en: Why the two loaves are chametz

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the two loaves of Shavuos are the only chametz offering, because chametz is the yetzer hara, and once the Torah comes into the world the yetzer hara can be refined and used for good. He brings 'I created the yetzer hara and created the Torah as its spice' and Moshe's answer to the angels.

title.en: Sefirah: counting down from chesed

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Sefirah refines the seven middos, since man contains all the powers of creation, and asks why the count begins with chesed, the highest, rather than malchus. He answers from the Midrash that the Avos and Moshe brought the Shechinah down step by step: Shavuos is not climbing to Heaven but bringing Heaven down.

title.en: Matzah, chametz and the Shavuos meal

summary.en: Returning to the Maharal, the Mashgiach contrasts Pesach, when the Jews were lifted up and ate only matzah, with Shavuos, when Heaven comes down and the refined chametz is offered. He explains why all agree that Shavuos requires eating, and why the only communal shelamim come with the two loaves.

title.en: 'Kedoshim tihyu': command and promise

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that parshas Kedoshim falls in the Sefirah weeks because its theme is the work of becoming holy, and that 'kedoshim tihyu' is both a command and a promise. He brings Rashi and the Ramban, the significance of the third week, and the Gemara that for a tzaddik going beyond the letter of the law becomes his law.

title.en: The Rozvadover's three 'Ani Hashem'

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Reb Moshe'le of Rozvadov, a grandson of the Ropshitzer, spoke on parshas Kedoshim before chassidim, simple people and mocking maskilim, applying each of the three 'Ani Hashem Elokeichem' to one group. He concludes that every person has a connection to Hashem according to his level.

title.en: From the Seder's gift to one's own work

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that 'kedoshim tihyu' is the theme running through Sefirah, rising each day to a higher holiness. On Pesach night Hashem lifted the Jews with a strong hand, but the next morning it is lost and the work begins, and he reads 'when your son asks you tomorrow' as the question of the morning after the Seder.

title.en: Using the middah of chesed for good

summary.en: The Mashgiach says man was created to sanctify himself through his own work, beginning with the middah of chesed, which must be used to love Hashem, Jews, tzaddikim and the Torah. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'chesed hu', and teaches that one's love of Hashem is measured by one's love of a fellow Jew.

title.en: The Stoliner Rebbe's chesed; help from Above

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of the Stoliner Rebbe in Williamsburg, a man of boundless chesed who hosted simple and far-off people, including a taxi driver at the Pesach Seder. He then explains the Midrash that opens Kedoshim with 'may He send your help from the Sanctuary': a person cannot sanctify himself alone, and Hashem helps.

title.en: Gratification and growing step by step

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a person needs some gratification, and that suddenly cutting off all pleasures leads to breakdown; one gives up a little at a time until one no longer needs it. He describes Jews whose pleasure is Torah and davening, and tells of Reb Nachum of Chernobyl, who his friends said grew stout from Torah.

oneLiner.en: Reading inside the Kedushas Levi and the Yesod Yosef, the Mashgiach explains that on Purim a new, heavenly light comes down into the natural world through the Megillah, through tzedakah and through the seudah, and that a person should receive it with preparation and simcha, not with drunkenness.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach continues from the previous week to give a sense of what Purim is, reading pieces of the Yesod Yosef and the Kedushas Levi inside so that the holy words reach the neshamah. Every Purim a new 'olam', a hidden world, comes down and stays ever new; it begins with the reading of the Megillah, a revealing of what was hidden. Purim is 'reishis', above the seven middos of this world, which is why Haman of Amalek, the reishis of tumah, fought Mordechai. Unlike Yom Kippur, when we rise to heaven, on Purim heaven descends into nature: the Megillah's miracles look natural, the names of Hashem hide in its words, and its reading purifies even the physical. The Mashgiach then speaks of preparing for the Megillah as a fresh start, of the special power of tzedakah on Purim, and closes by urging simcha without drunkenness, citing the Gemara, the Rema and a tzaddik whose 'drunkenness' came from the Megillah itself.

en: Every Purim a new, hidden 'olam' comes down to this world, and by its nature it stays new each year.
This light begins to come down with the reading of the Megillah, which reveals what was hidden, so one should answer amen to the brachah with great kavanah.
On Yom Kippur we rise up to heaven; on Purim heaven comes down into food, drink and the natural world.
The reading of the Megillah purifies even the physical world and the gashmiyus of whoever reads or hears it.
Tzedakah given on Purim is far more powerful than tzedakah during the year, and its flow of blessing reaches all the way down into this world.
The Mashgiach urges simcha on Purim without becoming drunk; the Megillah itself should be what makes a person 'drunk'.

title.en: Purim beyond our grasp; reading the sefarim inside

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is so sublime that the conscious mind cannot hold it, comparing it to pain beyond tolerance that needs an anesthetic. He introduces the Yesod Yosef, a kabbalistic sefer, and the Kedushas Levi, and explains why he will read them inside: written holy words pierce through gashmiyus into the neshamah.

title.en: A new world revealed through the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains 'olam' as something concealed, and says that on Purim a new olam comes down that stays new every year. It starts to come down with the reading of the Megillah, a 'revealing' of what was hidden, so one should answer amen to the brachah with great kavanah and stand ready to receive it.

title.en: Heaven on earth: Purim as reishis

summary.en: After noting that the Maharal hides kabbalah in plain words, the Mashgiach begins the Kedushas Levi: Purim brings 'days of heaven upon earth'. Purim is reishis, above the seven middos on which this world runs; Amalek is the reishis of tumah, and Haman sought the fiftieth level of tumah against Mordechai.

title.en: Purim and Yom Kippur; the obligation of the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Purim to Yom Kippur: on Yom Kippur we rise to heaven like malachim, on Purim heaven comes down into food and drink, so Purim is no 'Jewish Halloween'. From this he explains the Kedushas Levi's point that the obligation to hear the Megillah is stronger than that of Krias HaTorah, and likewise Parshas Zachor.

title.en: Hidden names and natural miracles

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the names of Hashem are hidden in the Megillah at its turning points, and its miracles all look like natural events. He tells how the Chiddushei HaRim pictured a man bringing news of Vashti into a beis medrash and being told to stop, not knowing it would become the Megillah. Then he reads the Kedushas Levi that through the Megillah the vitality of the spiritual comes down to be tasted in the natural world.

title.en: The Megillah purifies the physical

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the Megillah is read from a written scroll of parchment and ink: all of nature becomes purified, and the names in it light up in whoever reads or hears it and purify his gashmiyus. Unlike at Sinai, when the physical resisted the Torah, the Megillah purifies matter itself; a person should prepare for it by leaving the past behind.

title.en: A new beginning; this year's deeper descent

summary.en: Like Yom Kippur, the Megillah is a fresh start, and the Kedushas Levi writes that with every word a new light and a new malach come about. The Mashgiach adds that this year the Megillah's light must come down deeper than ever because the world has sunk lower, so wherever a person is, he should welcome it.

title.en: The special power of tzedakah on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tzedakah on Purim, matanos la'evyonim, is charged with far more power than all year: as a shadow mimics a person, Hashem gives to us as we give, and on Purim the shefa does not get stuck but reaches this world. He brings the Kedushas Levi's blessing that one who gives on Purim receives a thousandfold, and urges giving with simcha, personally, and training children to give.

title.en: Simcha without drunkenness

summary.en: Reading the Kedushas Levi's last paragraph against foolishness, the Mashgiach discusses drinking on Purim: the Gemara's 'ad delo yada', the story of Rabbah and Rav Zeira, the Rishonim's dispute and the Rema's 'a little more than usual'. He urges not becoming drunk, telling of a tzaddik who became 'drunk' from the Megillah itself, and closes with wishes for Shabbos and the geulah.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the seven weeks of Sefirah are like seven shemitos leading to yovel, the time when every Jewish soul returns to its root, and that yibum, Megillas Rus and even the berachah over bread are part of this same return.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the seven weeks of Sefirah as seven shemitos, with Shavuos as yovel, when every Jew returns to his inheritance. Moshe counted every soul, including future gilgulim, and a soul that did not complete its part of the Torah returns, as Megillas Rus shows: Machlon was brought back through Boaz's yibum and Oved, the root of Beis Dovid. Since the yeshivah is learning Yevamos, he explains its inner meaning through the Ramban on yibum and gilgul, and shows how Hashem guarded malchus Beis Dovid at every step. Through Rav Ashi's dream of Menashe, who taught where to break bread, he explains that Hashem fixes the 'first-baked part' first, and that hamotzi frees a soul's spark from the bread. He tells the Belzer Rav's story of the wheat, urges careful berachos and eating, and closes with the days of Sefirah as a tikkun leading to Matan Torah.

en: The seven weeks of Sefirah correspond to seven shemitos, and Shavuos is like yovel and Yom Kippur, the time when every Jew returns to his root.
Every Jew is a letter of the Torah; a soul that left the world without completing its mission returns through gilgul or yibum so that the Torah stays whole.
Megillas Rus is read on Shavuos because it is the story of yibum: Machlon's soul returned through Boaz and Rus as Oved, from whom came malchus Beis Dovid.
Masechta Yevamos is hard because learning it brings tikkun to souls cut off from their root, and whatever brings such tikkun meets obstacles.
Hashem fixes malchus Beis Dovid first, like the part of the bread that is baked first, and so He accepted Menashe's teshuvah against the middas hadin.
Food holds sparks of souls, and a berachah said with attention brings them their tikkun; therefore eating is a great responsibility.

title.en: Seven weeks as seven shemitos and yovel

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the seven weeks of Sefirah are seven shemitos and Shavuos is yovel, one with Yom Kippur, and that it is a time of freedom when every Jew returns to his inheritance.

title.en: Counted by Moshe; every Jew a letter of Torah

summary.en: Moshe counted all souls including future gilgulim; every Jew is a letter of the Torah, and one who did not complete his mission returns. The Mashgiach brings Megillas Rus: Machlon and Kilyon were earlier souls returning, and Machlon came back as Oved.

title.en: Return to the root; the cut branches of Shavuos

summary.en: Yom Kippur and Shavuos are times of return to the root, the Kisei Hakavod. The Mashgiach explains the custom of bringing trees in for Shavuos: the cut branches wilt, and one davens for Jewish souls cut off from their root.

title.en: Each Jew's nachalah and his share of Torah

summary.en: Each Jew's portion in Eretz Yisrael is his letter in the Torah and the source of his chiddushim. So Boaz, owner of the land, revealed the heter of a Moabite woman, while the closer relative, with no connection to it, refused Rus.

title.en: Why Masechta Yevamos is so hard

summary.en: Learning Yevamos deals with the tikkun of souls. Fixing oneself is hard and meets opposition, and what comes hard is a sign of one's mission; so too Yevamos is hard because, unknown to the learner, it brings tikkun to cut-off souls.

title.en: "Your wonders and thoughts are for us"

summary.en: From the Gemara in Yevamos about Dovid and Rechavam, the Mashgiach shows how Hashem guarded malchus Beis Dovid through every danger: Yehudah and Tamar, Boaz and Rus, and the Satan's claim, as with Esav, to a share of the holy soul.

title.en: Rus from Moav and the soul of Moshiach

summary.en: Rus came from Balak, who wanted to curse Israel, yet through Boaz came the blessing with Hashem's Name. Her soul was a branch cut off in Moav; Naomi, the Shechinah, went to gather it, beginning kibbutz galuyos with the soul of Moshiach himself.

title.en: The Ramban: yibum as the secret of gilgul

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban in Vayeshev that yibum is a great secret, meaning gilgul, and that his commentary on Iyov answers the suffering of the righteous through earlier lives. Rabbeinu Bachya states it openly; the closest relative can best bring the soul back.

title.en: Boaz, "a son to Naomi", and helping another Jew

summary.en: Continuing the Ramban, the Mashgiach explains that Boaz as closest relative could bring back Machlon, so the neighbors called Oved 'a son to Naomi'. He adds that every help to another Jew, learning with him or even answering amen, is a kind of yibum.

title.en: Dipping bread in vinegar: Menashe

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Shabbos that Boaz hinted to Rus about six tzaddikim, and that 'dip your bread in vinegar' meant Menashe. He asks why Boaz needed to tell her this, and introduces the Gemara in Sanhedrin about Rav Ashi and Menashe.

title.en: Menashe teaches where to break bread

summary.en: Menashe appears to Rav Ashi in a dream and teaches that one breaks bread where it is baked first. The Mashgiach concludes that Menashe became the teacher of all Israel for hamotzi, and this was Boaz's comfort to Rus: even the 'vinegar' would become a rav.

title.en: The tunnel under the Kisei Hakavod

summary.en: Menashe did teshuvah in captivity, and the Gemara says Hashem dug a tunnel under the Kisei Hakavod so the middas hadin could not block it. The Mashgiach explains that Menashe carried the spark of Moshiach, and Hashem's original plan for creation stands above the middas hadin.

title.en: The Belzer Rav and the fallen kugel

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how Rebbe Shalom of Belz had a piece of kugel that fell to the floor picked up and eaten, and told the story of a grain of wheat that prayed at every stage to be eaten with a berachah.

title.en: Sparks in food and the eleven melachos of bread

summary.en: Every food holds sparks of souls brought by hashgachah pratis, and a proper berachah gives them tikkun. Bread passes through eleven melachos, matching eleven levels of klipah, until baking, its last tikkun.

title.en: The first-baked place: malchus Beis Dovid

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks what Menashe knew that Rav Ashi did not, and answers that the part baked first is reaching its tikkun first by hashgachah. Malchus Beis Dovid, who must fix the world, is fixed first, like the Kohen Gadol who atones for himself first; hamotzi takes the spark out of the bread.

title.en: Eating as a battle: how to make hamotzi

summary.en: The ten words of hamotzi match the ten powers of the soul. Eating is a great responsibility, 'lechem' from 'milchamah'; the Mashgiach gives the parable of a relative pleading for attention and describes washing, cutting and dipping in salt with kavanah.

title.en: Boaz winnowing; Menashe's mother Chefzibah

summary.en: Boaz winnowed barley the night Rus came: of the three melachos of sorting, winnowing is done by the wind, by Hashem Himself, who refines malchus Beis Dovid. Menashe's mother was Chefzibah, 'My desire is in her'; only grain of Eretz Yisrael passes through all eleven melachos and receives a berachah.

title.en: Sefirah's tikkun and the night of Shavuos

summary.en: The days of Sefirah are a tikkun of the soul toward Shavuos. The Mashgiach brings the Kozhnitzer Maggid that even the last day can repair all fifty, the Zera Kodesh on Shavuos night, and says that today each Jew who takes on Torah is a lone individual, beloved to Hashem.

catalogTitle: הכנת עני לשבועות - שועתנו קבל ושמע צעקתנו

oneLiner.en: On the last day of sefirah the Mashgiach teaches that the true preparation for Shavuos is the cry of "shavaseinu kabel" from one who knows he is not ready, the power of tefillah shown in Megillas Ruth, and serving Hashem with freshness and seriousness.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach notes that Shavuos, unlike Pesach and Sukkos, has no physical preparation; its preparation is kedushah, unity and teshuvah, worked on through the days of sefirah. One who reaches the last week and sees how little he has achieved has the line of Ana Bekoach for that week: "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", a cry to Hashem who knows the hidden wish of every Jew to accept the Torah. Even the hagbalah at Sinai, knowing one may not go up, is itself a preparation. He then explains why Megillas Ruth is read on Shavuos: the Targum lists ten famines, the last a hunger to hear the word of Hashem before Moshiach, and Boaz ended his famine through tefillah; the megillah, the lineage of Dovid, the pillar of tefillah, comes to teach the power of prayer. He goes on to demand freshness and seriousness in avodah: Ruth against Orpah, Tosafos on kalus rosh at Matan Torah, no idle talk before davening, and davening with the tzibbur, and closes with a call to cry out on the last day of sefirah.

en: Shavuos has no physical preparation; its preparation is drawing kedushah onto oneself, unity among Jews and teshuvah, through the days of sefirah.

The line of Ana Bekoach for the last week of sefirah, "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", is the cry of one who is not prepared, relying on Hashem who knows the hidden wish of every Jew to accept the Torah.

Megillas Ruth is read on Shavuos to teach the power of tefillah: Boaz ended the famine through prayer, and the last famine, the hunger for the word of Hashem before Moshiach, will also be broken only by tefillah.
Avodas Hashem must stay fresh and not grow old or sleepy; the success of one's service depends on that freshness.
Seriousness is essential in avodah; lightheadedness (kalus rosh) is a great obstacle, and according to Tosafos it is what the Torah guarded against before Matan Torah.
Idle talk before davening ruins the whole tefillah, and coldness in one person spreads to others.

title.en: Preparing for Shavuos without an act

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Shavuos with Pesach and Sukkos, which require physical preparation, and explains that its preparation is kedushah, unity and teshuvah through sefirah. For one who reaches the last week unprepared he brings the line of Ana Bekoach, "shavaseinu kabel... yodea ta'alumos", a cry to Hashem who knows the hidden wish to accept the Torah.

title.en: The hagbalah and the last cry of sefirah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the three days of hagbalah, being held back from going up Har Sinai, teach a person to know he is not ready, and that this itself prepares him for the gift of Torah. The last week of sefirah is one great cry to Hashem, and its verse, "afsei aretz", shows that one reaches the lowest point and from there receives the Torah.

title.en: Coming to Shavuos like a convert

summary.en: From the middle branch of the menorah psalm the Mashgiach teaches that on Shavuos one should see himself as a goy about to convert, like Ruth, immersing at dawn for the sake of geirus. Shavuos is a mikveh, and the two loaves are Torah and tefillah, which depend on each other.

title.en: The fifth of Sivan, a day of tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the last day of sefirah, the fifth of Sivan when Jews said na'aseh v'nishma, a day of tefillah and kabbalas ol, a day to daven for one's share in Torah for the whole year. He explains that this is why Ruth, from whom Dovid the pillar of tefillah descends, is read on Shavuos.

title.en: The ten famines and the Targum on Ruth

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the opening of Megillas Ruth with the Targum's list of ten famines, the last of them a hunger to hear the word of Hashem before Moshiach, which he says we are living through. He shows that the Targum says twice that Boaz ended the famine through prayer, and asks why it repeats this and why the megillah mentions all ten famines.

title.en: Ruth teaches the power of tefillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Megillas Ruth, the lineage of Dovid the pillar of tefillah, comes to teach the power of prayer: the tenth and strongest famine will be stilled only by tefillah. The megillah is a psak written by Shmuel, and a psak restates its reason at the end, so the Targum repeats Boaz's prayer.

title.en: Staying warm and fresh in avodah

summary.en: After asking the listeners to daven for a sick friend, the Mashgiach speaks of unity and of warming one another, since what is not kept warm grows cold. He brings that all of Moshe Rabbeinu's ascents came through rising early, that a kos shel brachah must be fresh, and that the chevra was founded on warm davening, and demands that every day be like new.

title.en: Ruth and Orpah: freshness and seriousness

summary.en: The Mashgiach compares Ruth and Orpah: both accepted the yoke of Heaven, but only Ruth's acceptance stayed fresh and lasting, and from her came Dovid while from Orpah came Golias. He then demands seriousness against lightheadedness, entering shul with joy and not talking during davening.

title.en: Tosafos: kalus rosh at Matan Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara in Shabbos on the three days of separation before Matan Torah, and Tosafos' question why a ba'al keri could not receive the Torah before there was any tumah. Following Tosafos' second answer, he explains that the concern was kalus rosh, since Torah must be received with awe and trembling.

title.en: Coffee and talk before davening

summary.en: The Mashgiach says coffee before davening is for strength, not for settling down to chat and joke, and that talk before davening ruins the tefillah. He tells of a tzaddik who shared his bread in a concentration camp and from whose way of drinking coffee one could learn yiras shamayim, and brings the Gemara's reasoning that some could not have been immersing while others were receiving the Torah.

title.en: Davening with toil and with the tzibbur

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the hanhagos printed at the end of Noam Elimelech, not to speak before davening, and says the Ba'al Shem Tov re-established the pillar of tefillah. He describes how Ahavah Rabbah once took two hours, brings Rashi that a blessing must not be said in haste but with a full heart, and warns of the danger of davening alone rather than with the tzibbur.

title.en: Shavuos night and the final cry

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains, with the Zohar and Midrash Tanchuma, that Shavuos is a mikveh and that staying up all night with toil in Torah shows willing acceptance of the Oral Torah that was once accepted under compulsion. He returns to "shavaseinu kabel" as the last cry of sefirah, brings the Kozhnitzer Maggid that the last day can make up all fifty, and closes with brachos.

catalogTitle: מקבלים תורה מחדש; נחיצות הכנה לשבועות; לא לעשות מעיקר טפל ומטפל עיקר; לשפוך נפשו באהבה רבה

oneLiner.en: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Mashgiach teaches that Matan Torah truly returns every year, that Shavuos is named for its preparation, and that one must not let the night's vigil ruin the morning's davening and Krias HaTorah, the heart of receiving the Torah.

abstract.en: Opening with Rashi on the Jews' arrival at Sinai on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, the Mashgiach explains that every Yom Tov repeats itself each year, comparing the year to a rotating card file where each day's card comes round again. Matan Torah therefore happens every year: tzaddikim like the Belzer Rav see it, and even coarse people's souls receive it, as a numbed tooth is worked on without feeling. Because the Yom Tov is named Shavuos after the weeks of preparation, the Mashgiach stresses teshuvah on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, unity, the special Shavuos mikveh and a heartfelt Ahavah Rabbah. He warns against making the main thing secondary: staying up all night and then sleeping through davening, Krias HaTorah and the Kedushah of Musaf, like a chassan who spent on everything but forgot the ring. He closes with the rare reading of Naso before Shavuos and a prayer for salvation.

en: Every Yom Tov repeats itself each year, like a card on a rotating wheel that comes round again, so Matan Torah truly happens every Shavuos.
Great tzaddikim perceive Matan Torah as it was at Sinai; others feel it according to their level, and even those who feel nothing still receive it in their soul.
The Yom Tov is called Shavuos, after the weeks of preparation, because the preparation is so central that it gives the Yom Tov its name.
The preparation includes teshuvah from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, unity among Jews, and the special mikveh of Shavuos morning.
Staying awake all night must not come at the cost of davening, Krias HaTorah and the Kedushah of Musaf, which are the main thing of Shavuos.
A Jew's success in learning all year comes from Shavuos, and Ahavah Rabbah on Shavuos should be said with an outpouring of the heart.

title.en: Each Yom Tov comes round again

summary.en: On Rosh Chodesh Sivan the Mashgiach brings Rashi that the arrival at Sinai was in teshuvah, then explains that every Yom Tov repeats itself yearly, comparing the year to a rotating card file. Therefore Matan Torah happens every year.

title.en: Seeing Matan Torah: the Shinever Rav

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Shinever Rav wanted to travel to Belz to experience Matan Torah, and his father the Sanzer Rav showed it to him at home. He explains that each Jew experiences Matan Torah by his level, likening those who feel nothing to a numbed tooth, and that all of Sefirah prepares for the reading of the Aseres HaDibros.

title.en: A Yom Tov named for its preparation

summary.en: The Mashgiach says no mitzvah is prepared for like Shavuos, and that the Yom Tov is named for the weeks of preparation rather than for the Torah. He calls for teshuvah from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, as Rashi teaches, and for the unity of 'one heart' that preceded Matan Torah.

title.en: The Shavuos mikveh and Ahavah Rabbah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a mikveh, like a sukkah, is holy through the holy names that the halachos bring into it, and that the mikveh of Shavuos morning is a different kind of mikveh. He adds that Pesukei Dezimra and Ahavah Rabbah of Shavuos are part of the preparation, recalling how long Ahavah Rabbah took in Tsanz.

title.en: The vigil and the forgotten ring

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns against staying up all night and then dozing through davening and the Kedushah of Musaf, where the great union takes place, citing the Ropshitzer, the Ba'al Shem Tov and the Minchas Elazar. He compares it to a chassan who paid for everything at the wedding but forgot the ring.

title.en: The Ahavas Yisroel and the main thing

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Ahavas Yisroel of Vizhnitz sent a group of yeshiva students to sleep so that they could daven properly, and says that one who knows a short rest will not suffice should not stay up Shavuos night. He mentions the Imrei Emes's takanah to daven early and repeats: do not make the main thing secondary.

title.en: Shavuos as a day of judgment; tears at Ahavah Rabbah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that one should fear Shavuos more than Rosh Hashanah, since then one is judged on Torah and mitzvos, and a bochur's success in learning all year comes from it. He calls for Ahavah Rabbah with tears, and returns to teshuvah on Rosh Chodesh Sivan, which contains the whole of Shavuos.

title.en: Parshas Naso before Shavuos; a prayer for salvation

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that this year Parshas Naso is read before Shavuos, which almost never happens, and suggests it may be so that the merit of the twelve nesi'im should nullify the twelve princes of Yishmael at a time of danger. He ties Shavuos to Moshiach through Dovid HaMelech and the Ba'al Shem Tov, and closes with a call to use the coming days and a blessing to receive the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: המן- The Architect of his Own Demise

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows that in the Megillah, where Hashem hides His face, Haman himself prepared every step of his own downfall, and that Amalek's attack on 'the end' fails because the Jewish people have no end.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the twelve months, which correspond to the twelve tribes arranged in four camps. Nisan, the month of Yehuda and of the miracles of Egypt, comes first; the months descend until Adar, the last, whose Megillah has no open miracle at all. This is hester panim: Hashem hides, yet controls everything, and every small story in the Megillah is a wheel in one mechanism. The Mashgiach reads Chazal's identification of Memuchan with Haman as a signal to watch Haman, who unknowingly prepared Esther's rise, Mordechai's honor, his house and his own gallows. Adar means a cloak, and Dan is the last and most removed tribe, yet his son Chushim killed Esav. Amalek attacks those at the end, outside the camp, as Haman rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar; but the Jewish people have no end, and Purim protects those at the end.

en: The months descend from Nisan, named for its miracles, to Adar, whose Megillah contains no open miracle at all.
The message of the Megillah is that even when no miracles are seen, Hashem is hidden but controls everything.
Haman prepared every element of his own downfall: Vashti's removal, Mordechai's honor, his house and the gallows.
Dan, the last tribe, is the most removed from holiness and always gets into trouble, yet he remains connected to the Shem Havayah.
Amalek attacks those at the end, outside the camp, and Haman likewise hoped to prevail in Adar, the month of the end.
The Jewish people have no end: Amalek has an end, but when the Jews finish they begin again.

candidateTopics: leadership in the generation before Moshiach

title.en: Twelve months, twelve tribes, and Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach matches the twelve months to the twelve tribes in their four camps, from Nisan and Yehuda to Adar at the end. He notes that Amalek has no future, and that the months descend from Nisan's miracles to Adar's Megillah, where no open miracle appears.

title.en: Hidden face: Haman prepares everything

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara's source for Esther in the Torah, hester panim, and explains that every small story in the Megillah is a wheel in one mechanism. From Chazal's identification of Memuchan with Haman he shows that Haman prepared Vashti's removal, Mordechai's greatness and his own gallows.

title.en: Only Haman knew how to do it

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls it a mockery of avodah zarah that it prepares its own demise. Mordechai, a tzaddik with rachmanus and no taste for honor, could not have devised the cruel gallows, the royal honor or the mansion; Haman did all three, unknowingly for Mordechai.

title.en: Adar the cloak; Dan and Chushim

summary.en: Returning to the months, the Mashgiach explains that Adar means a cloak, as with Esav's mantle of hair: the miracles are covered. Dan, the last and most removed tribe, still bears a permutation of the Shem Havayah, and it was Dan's son Chushim, deaf and mute, who killed Esav at Yaakov's burial.

title.en: The last generation: hester panim today

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls the generation before Moshiach a generation of Chushim and of great hester panim. He recalls that in his youth there were universally accepted leaders, the last being the Chazon Ish, while today great men are accepted only by their own factions.

title.en: Amalek attacks the end; Adar Sheini

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that those of Dan expelled from the camp were outside the Clouds of Glory, so Amalek could strike the stragglers. Haman, like Amalek, rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar, the month of the end, and a leap year's Adar Sheini, likened to the last eight pesukim of the Torah, seemed even more outside the camp. His mistake: these too belong to the camp.

title.en: No end for Yidden; Shushan Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that the Jews have no end: when they finish the Torah they begin Bereishis again, and Purim protects those at the end of the camp. He then speaks of the special holiness of Shushan Purim, kept today only in Yerushalayim, and of his plan to be there.

catalogTitle: אנכי ה' - האמונה למעלה מן השכל בחורים צעירים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the fiftieth day, on which the Torah and 'Anochi Hashem' were given, is above time, number and intellect, and that the emunah received there is what a Jew in the last generation must hold on to, driving out every thought of doubt.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with three questions about Shavuos: we count only forty-nine days, Moshe added a day of his own, and we say 'the time of the giving of our Torah' on a day it was not given. He answers that the fiftieth day is above number and above this world, like the place of the aron that took up no space, and like the Torah, whose pesukim do not fit a count. 'Anochi Hashem' was given above intellect, and that is emunah, which is higher than knowledge. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that before Moshiach Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which is apikorsus, and says the task of this generation is simple faith. He speaks openly to bachurim troubled by doubts: the pain shows they believe, and driving such a thought out fulfills the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru'. With the parable of a building's main switch he shows how much each mitzvah and each sin does above.

en: The fiftieth day is above number and above the seven-day order of the world, so it cannot be counted, and by Heaven's reckoning the day Moshe chose is still the fiftieth.
'Anochi Hashem Elokecha' was given above intellect, time and place, and so it is received as emunah, which is higher than knowledge.
Before Moshiach Jews are pulled into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which is apikorsus, and the task of this generation is to hold on to simple faith in Hashem and in the whole Torah.
Doubts that torment a person are not real doubts but a confusion of the mind, and his pain is itself a sign that he believes.
Even the greatest tzaddik has a moment of doubt, so that he can fulfill the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru' by driving the thought out.
A person does not know his own power: each of his limbs is a switch, and a mitzvah lights up all the worlds while a sin brings destruction.

title.en: Three questions on the fiftieth day

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the count is called fifty but only forty-nine days are counted, how Moshe could add a day, and why the first day of Shavuos is called the time of the giving of the Torah, especially in Eretz Yisrael. He begins to answer that the fiftieth day is above number, which belongs only to this world.

title.en: Above the world, above time and place

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the world was made in seven days and the eighth week and fiftieth day are above it, so by Heaven's reckoning the day Moshe chose is the fiftieth. He compares it to the Kodesh HaKodashim, where the aron took up no space.

title.en: Anochi Hashem: emunah above knowledge

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the Masorah's count of pesukim in parshas Yisro does not fit, because the Torah is above time and number. 'Anochi Hashem' was given above intellect, the redemption was completed on the fiftieth day, and that is why it is received as emunah, which is higher than knowledge.

title.en: The fiftieth gate and simple faith

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ohr HaChaim that before Moshiach Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate of impurity, which he identifies as apikorsus, spread today as never before. The task of the generation is simple faith in Hashem and in the whole Torah, its sages and their chiddushim, which those who learn lishmah see come with heavenly help.

title.en: Bachurim troubled by doubts

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of bachurim and older people who come to him troubled by doubts in emunah, and explains why he speaks about it: such doubts can befall anyone, often through pegamim. He says their pain shows that they believe, and that these are not real doubts but a confusion of the mind, like a person who keeps going back to check that the door is locked.

title.en: Driving out the thought: velo sasuru

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that every Jew, even the greatest tzaddik, has a moment of doubt, so that he can fulfill the mitzvah of 'velo sasuru acharei levavchem'. Bringing the Bnei Yissaschar and the Tanya, he explains that one should not feel bad when such a thought comes, since it comes from the yetzer hara, and driving it out is one of the greatest mitzvos, especially now when the fiftieth gate must be broken.

title.en: The main switch: a person's hidden power

summary.en: The Mashgiach says no person knows how important he is: his 248 limbs and 365 sinews are like buttons, as one push of the main switch lights the whole Empire State Building. A mitzvah lights up all the worlds and a sin like eating treif sets off destruction; he brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that a person must be told his strength, and the elephant that fears a fly.

title.en: Heavenly lamps and the week of malchus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew who drives out a thought of doubt can save thousands of Jews, and brings the Maggid's reading that everything above comes from you. He describes each Jew's 248 heavenly lamps, brighter the greater he is, mentions Reb Mordechai of Chernobyl who passed away in the week of malchus, and closes with a brachah to receive the Torah with joy, love and fear of Hashem.

catalogTitle: הוא היצה"ר הוא השטן הוא ה"היינטיגע וועלט" איך זה נלמד מענינא דיומא

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains, from a saying of the Chasam Sofer and from Megillas Ruth, that 'today's world' is simply the newest name of the yetzer hara and the Satan, and that only firm separation from it carries a Jew through to Kabbalas HaTorah and Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a saying of the Chasam Sofer, heard through Rabbi Aharon Pollak: the yetzer hara's firm went bankrupt, reopened as 'Satan', and now trades under the name 'today's world'. He applies it to the son of the Egyptian, whose mother Shlomis greeted everyone, and to Akdamus, where Knesses Yisrael, the Shulamis, refuses the nations' invitation and wants only the separate camps of the desert. From Megillas Ruth he shows that the root of Moshiach was hidden in a generation of chutzpah and immorality, like the signs of ikvesa d'meshicha at the end of Sotah, and contrasts Ruth's honor for her mother-in-law with today's ideal of independence. From Rashi on the neighbors of Korach and of Moshe he shows how lasting an influence is. He calls for being 'extreme', saying 'I am a chassid', and closes with preparing from Rosh Chodesh Sivan for Kabbalas HaTorah.

en: According to the Chasam Sofer, the yetzer hara keeps changing its name, from yetzer hara to Satan to 'today's world', and a Jew held back from Hashem's will by 'today's world' should know it is the same firm.
Knesses Yisrael is the 'Shulamis', whose peace is within her own camp, unlike Shlomis bas Divri, who greeted everyone and let a foreign culture in.
Megillas Ruth describes a generation of chutzpah and immorality because the root of Moshiach was hidden there so that the Satan, who fears Moshiach, would not suspect it.
The neighbors one lives among shape a person for generations, as Rashi shows from the neighbors of Korach and of Moshe and Aharon.
The Mashgiach says the only way to withstand today's world is to separate from it and be 'extreme', to say openly 'I am a chassid'.
Matan Torah repeats every year, and from Rosh Chodesh Sivan one should follow, day by day, what happened then at Har Sinai.

candidateTopics: today's world as the yetzer hara

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: the firm that changed its name

summary.en: After a word on preparing to speak, the Mashgiach tells how Rabbi Aharon Pollak heard from an elderly rebbetzin, a descendant of the Chasam Sofer, about his Shabbos-day mussar talks. Once the Chasam Sofer said that the yetzer hara's firm went bankrupt, reopened as 'Satan', and now calls itself 'today's world'.

title.en: Shlomis bas Divri and the son of the Egyptian

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the man of Dan objected to the son of the Egyptian pitching his tent in the camp, when the desert was wide. He answers from Rashi that his mother Shlomis greeted everyone, and the neighbor did not want her 'today's world' brought to his children.

title.en: Akdamus: Shulamis versus Shlomis

summary.en: From Akdamus and the Midrash on 'Shuvi shuvi haShulamis', the Mashgiach describes the nations inviting Knesses Yisrael into their society, and her answer that they cannot give her the separate camps of the desert. He contrasts Shlomis, who reaches out with peace to all, with Shulamis, whose peace is within her own walls.

title.en: Why Megillas Ruth tells of a corrupt generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads 'the days when the judges were judged' and Boaz sleeping at the edge of the grain heap, and asks why a megillah whose purpose is to establish David's lineage needs these details. He begins to answer that the Satan fears Moshiach, so Hashem hides every root of Moshiach.

title.en: Chutzpah and the hidden root of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the signs of ikvesa d'meshicha at the end of Sotah and explains that the ruling permitting a Moabite woman was a turning point for Moshiach, so it was hidden in a generation of chutzpah and immorality. In such a world Boaz noticed Ruth's tznius.

title.en: Ruth's honor for her mother-in-law

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how Ruth, a princess of Moav, left everything to follow and serve her mother-in-law, against the sign of the end of days that a bride rises against her mother-in-law. He contrasts this with today's ideal of independence from parents and authority, and says the way to survive is separation, not greeting everyone.

title.en: The neighbor's influence lasts a thousand years

summary.en: From Rashi on the camps around the Mishkan, the Mashgiach shows that Reuven's neighbors learned from Korach while Yissachar, next to Moshe and Aharon, produced two hundred heads of Sanhedrin almost a thousand years later. He applies this to the pull of television and trends and to the broken families that come to him, all from 'today's world'.

title.en: Be 'extreme': I am a chassid

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls for separation, citing Yeshayahu's 'go into your rooms and shut your door', the Lubavitcher's blessing to be healthy, fresh and 'meshuga', and the Kotzker's advice to say 'I am a chassid'. He argues that today's world is the truly extreme one and describes what he saw in bungalow colonies as a young man and what goes on there now.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh Sivan: arriving at Har Sinai

summary.en: With Rosh Chodesh Sivan that night, the Mashgiach brings 'on this day they came to the desert of Sinai' and that leaving Refidim was with teshuvah, and the Avodas Yisrael's practice of learning each day what happened then. He explains that Matan Torah repeats every year, and brings the Rimanover that the five days before it were spent saying Ahavah Rabbah.

title.en: Preparing for Shavuos; closing blessing

summary.en: The Mashgiach urges good learning and davening in the days before Shavuos and remembering Matan Torah from Rosh Chodesh on. He closes by blessing the listeners to stay healthy, fresh and settled, knowing that it is today's world that is mad, and to receive the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: פרה אדומה - A מצוה that is Above our Understanding

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah Adumah, the chok no one can understand, is the cure for the sin of Adam HaRishon, who wanted to understand beyond his reach, and that its lesson of faith and waiting prepares the Jewish people for Nisan and the Geulah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the halachos of Parah Adumah: since we have no red heifer, all are tamei, yet hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah. He links Parah to Purim: Purim comforts those left outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and brings them in, preparing for Parshas HaChodesh and Nisan. On Rosh Chodesh Nisan the Satan argues that the Jews are unworthy of redemption; Parah, a chok done without reason, answers that Hashem may redeem without reason. He traces tumah to the Nachash, who is the Satan, and to Adam and Chava's desire for intellect beyond their reach, which brought death, the highest tumah, into the world. Doing a mitzvah without understanding is the tikkun. Two things are closed to the mind: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. Judaism is built on waiting, since the first sin, the golden calf and Shaul's failure were all failures to wait, while Dovid waited.

en: Without a red heifer everyone today is tamei from contact with the dead, but hearing Parshas Parah removes the inner tumah that blocks a person from kedushah.
Parshas Parah completes Purim: Purim comforts those outside the camp, while Parah purifies them and lets them enter.
Parah, a chok kept without understanding, answers the Satan's claim on Rosh Chodesh Nisan that the Jews have no reason to be redeemed.
Death, brought by the sin of the Eitz HaDaas, is itself tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to the venom of the Nachash.
The sin of Adam was wanting to understand beyond his reach, and doing a mitzvah without understanding is its tikkun.
Judaism is built on waiting, because the first sin was a failure to wait.

candidateTopics: Rosh Chodesh Nisan and the Geulah

title.en: Tumah today and the reading of Parah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the red heifer and explains that without it everyone today is tamei and cannot go up on Har HaBayis. He says that hearing Parshas Parah with faith removes the inner tumah, as a body has a neshamah, so tumah has an outer and an inner part.

title.en: Parah as the completion of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach ties Parah to Pur through the gematria and brings that Parshas Parah continues Purim, since Shabbos lifts up the week. Purim saves those expelled from the camp but leaves them outside; Parah purifies them and brings them in, so they enter Parshas HaChodesh renewed.

title.en: Nisan and the Satan's accusation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Nisan is the month of birth and redemption, and that on Rosh Chodesh Nisan kings are appointed in Heaven. The good malachim move that Hashem become King and Moshiach come, but the Satan argues the Jews are not worthy and the matter is put off.

title.en: A chok beyond understanding answers the Satan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parah is a chok that even Shlomo HaMelech could not understand, and that keeping it shows Klal Yisrael's deep emunah. Since Jews do a mitzvah without a reason, Hashem can redeem them without a reason. Parshas Parah is the deepest Shabbos of the year, the last one feeding the week of Adar.

title.en: The Nachash, the Satan and the lure of intellect

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks where the yetzer hara comes from and explains that Adam and Chava had no inner desires before the sin. The Nachash and the Satan are one, as their gematria shows; he could only tempt them with higher understanding, the knowledge of good and bad.

title.en: Death is tumah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that death, the punishment for the sin, is really tumah, which is why a corpse is the highest level of tumah. Life is the G-dliness in a person; the malach hamaves pulls it out and injects tumah, and Parah Adumah is the antidote to that venom.

title.en: A mitzvah without understanding as the tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that tumas meis came because Adam and Chava wanted understanding beyond them, so its cure is a mitzvah done without understanding. Understanding is a fringe benefit, not a condition for keeping mitzvos; Parah brings life, as its mayim chaim and the passuk about the tzaddik living by his emunah show.

title.en: Two closed doors: Parah and the time of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach says we are in ikvesa d'meshicha and names two things the mind may not enter: how Parah works and when Moshiach will come. He brings Yaakov Avinu, Daniel and Achashverosh's miscalculation, and compares the Jews' disappointment then to the disappointment after the Holocaust.

title.en: Judaism is built on waiting

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew must wait, and contrasts a gentile served breakfast in bed with a Jew who must wash, daven and make hamotzi before eating. He brings the Ohr HaChaim that the Eitz HaDaas was a vine whose grapes Adam was meant to keep for Kiddush on Shabbos, so the first sin was not waiting.

title.en: The egel, Shaul and Dovid: waiting for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at Matan Torah death could have ended, but the golden calf came from not waiting for Moshe Rabbeinu. Shaul lost his kingdom for not waiting for Shmuel, while Dovid waited for the sound in the treetops, so Moshiach comes from him. He ends that waiting for Moshiach is waiting for the world to be sprinkled with Parah.

catalogTitle: טעמים לאכילת מאכלי חלב. התעוררות לחג

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why the angels at Avraham's table were faulted for eating meat with milk and why milk is eaten on Shavuos, then teaches that every Jew is a letter in the Sefer Torah that Hashem writes anew each Shavuos, and that one prepares for it by making oneself clean and knowing that one is nothing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the rewards the Mishnah in Avos promises one who learns Torah lishmah: counsel, kingship, the secrets of the Torah, and greatness over all creation, which he illustrates with stories of the Ba'al Shem Tov and of a wagon driver of the Stoliner Rebbe. From the angels' fear of Moshe he turns to the Midrash that Moshe silenced them by recalling that they ate meat and milk at Avraham's table, and asks how, since Rashi says the milk came first. Using the Chesed LeAvraham, a stringency of the Beis Yosef, and the Igros Sofrim's teaching that meat is din and milk a higher chesed, he resolves it through the argument over whether the upper or the lower prevails. He then explains milk on Shavuos, the renewal of the Torah each year, every Jew as a letter of the Sefer Torah reflected in the counting and camps of Bamidbar, and preparation through purity, humility and the strength of individuals.

en: The Mashgiach explains from the Mishnah in Avos that one who learns Torah lishmah is given counsel, a kingship that draws people to him, the secrets of the Torah, and greatness over all creation, even angels.
Meat is din and milk is chesed drawn from Binah, so meat after milk is permitted while milk after meat is not, because the lower food prevails.
Milk is eaten on Shavuos because the days of sefirah, days of din, have ended, and red has turned to white, din to chesed.
Each Shavuos the Torah is truly given again from heaven, and Hashem writes a new Sefer Torah in which every Jewish soul is a letter.
The preparation is to make oneself like clean white parchment, refining the animal side of the person, so the black fire of Hashem's letters can rest on it.
The Torah was given in the wilderness: knowing that one is nothing is the greatest preparation for receiving it.
In a generation where only individuals keep the Torah, each individual carries the Torah for all of Klal Yisrael.
