din and chesed in meat and milk
Shavuos as a renewed giving of the Torah
every Jew as a letter in the Sefer Torah
Parshas Bamidbar and the counting of Israel
the individual in a weak generation

title.en: The rewards of Torah lishmah

summary.en: The Mashgiach goes through the Mishnah in Avos on one who learns Torah lishmah: people draw counsel from him, he is given kingship and the secrets of the Torah, he becomes like a spring that grows stronger, and the Torah raises him above all creation.

title.en: Stories of a tzaddik's hidden power

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Ba'al Shem Tov saw that a shake of the Mishneh LaMelech's head cast down the heavenly minister of Russia, and how a wagon driver of the Stoliner Rebbe crossed breaking ice after calling out the name of a family. The heavenly ministers over roads, seas and ice tremble before one who learns Torah lishmah.

title.en: Did the angels eat meat with milk?

summary.en: From the angels' fear of Moshe, the Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Moshe answered them by recalling that they ate meat and milk at Avraham's table, and asks how, since Rashi says the milk came first. He brings the Chesed LeAvraham that the calf was made through Sefer Yetzirah and is not meat, and is left with two questions: why the angels were at fault, and why Avraham was not.

title.en: Din, chesed, and Moshe's answer to the angels

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers that Avraham kept a stringency of not eating meat after milk in one meal, but without bread these were two meals. He brings the Igros Sofrim that meat is din and milk a strong chesed from Binah, so meat may follow milk since the lower prevails, and ties this to the argument between Moshe, who held that the lower prevails, and the angels, who held that the upper does.

title.en: Milk on Shavuos and the Torah given anew

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the reasons of the Rema and the Magen Avraham for eating milk on Shavuos: the days of sefirah are days of din, and as blood turns to milk, red turns to white. He then says that each Shavuos the Torah is truly given again, tells how the Shinever Rav saw it in Belz, and brings that the Shabbos before Shavuos contains all of Shavuos.

title.en: Bamidbar: every Jew is a letter

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Parshas Bamidbar is read before Shavuos: it counts the Jews, and every Jew has a letter in the Sefer Torah, as the word Yisrael hints. He brings the Arizal on seeing one's letter, the early sofrim who counted the letters, and Rabbi Akiva who expounded the crowns of each letter.

title.en: White parchment for Hashem's new Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each Shavuos Hashem writes a new Sefer Torah, and no festival has as much preparation as Shavuos, from the counting of sefirah to Rosh Chodesh Sivan. He asks why a Sefer Torah must be written on an animal's hide and answers that the animal side of a person must be refined into clean white parchment for Hashem's black fire.

title.en: Counting by the root of the soul; the camps as a Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that only Moshe, Aharon and the nesi'im could count the Jews, because they saw each one's root and his letter in the Torah. The camps matched the books of the Torah with the Levi'im in the middle like Vayikra; an extra letter invalidates a Sefer Torah, which explains the incident of the blasphemer; and the 22,000 Levi'im, counted from thirty days, match the 22 letters.

title.en: Wilderness humility and the power of the individual

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the work of the Shabbos before Shavuos is to become clean by knowing one is nothing, since the Torah was given in the wilderness; he brings the Kozhnitzer that the fifty days can still be repaired at the last minute. He explains that the commandments were said in the singular so the Torah would endure through individuals, and says that today each individual must know his duty.

title.en: Receiving the Torah for the whole year

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads a passage on the hardships before Moshiach, when even rabbanim will need mercy to stay in emunah, and says that each Shavuos one receives the Torah for the whole year. He speaks of the purity of the night of Shavuos and the custom of going to the mikveh, of sleep and learning, and closes with a brachah.

catalogTitle: “זכור את יום אשר עמדת לפני ה' אלוקיך בחורב”

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains the Torah's warning never to forget the day the Jewish people stood before Hashem at Chorev, and how that day returns every Shavuos to be received anew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the pesukim in Devarim warning, in several expressions, not to forget the day at Chorev and to tell it to one's children: Har Sinai, where every Jew heard Hashem speak, is the foundation of emunah. He explains that every event in the Torah is engraved in its time, so each year the same lights return, and on Shavuos matan Torah comes down again, as tzaddikim visibly relived it; sin only insulates the body from feeling it. The avodah of Shavuos is to become a vessel for the Torah, especially at Ahavah Rabbah and the reading of the Aseres Hadibros. With the mashal of a chasan who pays for everything but forgets the ring, he warns against sleeping through the main moment after a night awake. He tells of the Belzer Rav's heart before Shavuos and the Satmar Rav's reading, stresses the worth of avodah in a polluted generation, and closes with the Midrash on the horns of Yitzchak's ram and a plea for mercy on all Jews.

en: The Torah warns in many expressions not to forget the day at Chorev, because Har Sinai, where every Jew heard Hashem, is the foundation of emunah passed on to the generations.
Every event in the Torah is engraved in its time, so each year the same lights return, and on Shavuos matan Torah comes down again.
The avodah of Shavuos is to be a vessel to receive the Torah, above all at the reading of the Aseres Hadibros, when every Jew stands at Har Sinai.
Staying awake all night is worthless if one then sleeps through Ahavah Rabbah and the reading of the Aseres Hadibros.
In a generation whose spiritual air is polluted, a Jew who struggles to learn and daven is doing something very great and precious to Hashem.
Having heard the left horn of the ram at Sinai, the Mashgiach asks that we soon hear the right horn, the shofar of Moshiach, and that Hashem have mercy on Jews everywhere.

candidateTopics: Har Sinai as the foundation of emunah
the annual return of the Yomim Tovim
Shavuos night and the Aseres Hadibros
avodah in a spiritually polluted generation

title.en: Do not forget the day at Chorev

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the pesukim in Devarim that warn, in several expressions, not to forget the day the people stood before Hashem at Chorev and to tell it to one's children. He explains that Har Sinai, where every Jew became a prophet and heard Hashem speak face to face, is the foundation of emunah and of the belief in Moshe Rabbeinu.

title.en: The same lights return every year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that everything in the Torah is engraved in its time like a circle, so each year the same lights return; this is why a year is called shanah, repetition. Tzaddikim such as the Sanzer Rav and Reb Sholom of Belz visibly relived matan Torah, and the Mashgiach says sin is like insulation that keeps the body from feeling what the soul experiences.

title.en: The avodah of Shavuos: becoming a vessel

summary.en: Every Yom Tov has its avodah, and the avodah of Shavuos is to become a vessel for the day at Chorev, which one must remember daily through the Six Remembrances or Ahavah Rabbah. The main receiving is at the reading of the Aseres Hadibros; the Mashgiach cites a Rebbe that one should fear Shavuos more than Rosh Hashanah, and describes the thunder and trembling at Sinai and the prayer for more Torah.

title.en: The chasan who forgot the ring

summary.en: The Mashgiach gives the mashal of a chasan who pays for everything at the wedding but refuses to buy the ring needed for the kiddushin, and compares him to one who stays up all Shavuos night and then sleeps through Ahavah Rabbah and the Aseres Hadibros. He advises resting a few hours before davening, and that one who knows he will fall asleep should not stay up all night.

title.en: The Belzer Rav's heart and a polluted generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how the Belzer Rav answered the king's doctor, who found his heart beating irregularly, that in six days it would be Shavuos, and recalls hearing the Satmar Rav read the Aseres Hadibros. Today we do not feel this, but since the physical air and water are polluted, so is the spiritual atmosphere, and a Jew who struggles to learn and daven in it is very precious.

title.en: The right horn of the ram and a plea for mercy

summary.en: From the Selichos prayer and the Midrash that the left horn of Yitzchak's ram was the shofar of Sinai and the right horn will be the shofar of Moshiach, the Mashgiach asks that we soon hear the right horn. He lists the dangers facing Jews in Eretz Yisroel, Russia and Iran, calls to pray for mercy on Shavuos, and urges coming to learn before davening and receiving the Torah with joy.

catalogTitle: כל יהודי הוא שליח מה'; שמירת עינים בימי הקיץ

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew is Hashem's messenger wherever he goes, and that the summer travel of Tamuz and Av is meant to repair the failed mission of the meraglim, above all by guarding the eyes and by tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the meraglim, who set out on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz and returned on Tisha b'Av after failing their mission, and contrasts them with the successful messengers Yehoshua sent. He then asks why the whole world travels in exactly these weeks. Bringing the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'From Hashem are a man's steps established', he explains that every soul is sent down as a messenger, and that each person has a portion of creation that only he can repair: a glass of water in Chicago or a tree in the country has waited since creation for his brachah or his learning. Since the meraglim sinned with their eyes, these weeks are full of tests for the eyes; the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of Bilaam's blind eye shows that forbidden sights blind a person to the light of Torah. The Mashgiach stresses tefillah for success, with a story of a tzaddik's Pesach, and calls on bochurim to keep learning and kabbalas ol in the summer, to see Hashem's creation, and so turn these months into joy.

en: According to the Ba'al Shem Tov, every person is a messenger of Hashem, and wherever he goes he has been sent there to do something.
The summer travel season falls in the meraglim's forty days, and a Jew's travels in these weeks are meant to repair what they spoiled.
Each person has his own portion of creation that only he can repair, through mitzvos and brachos, and spoil through aveiros.
The eyes are the most sensitive and holiest part of the body; one who looks at forbidden things can no longer see the light and sweetness of Torah.
Success in one's mission requires tefillah: the meraglim failed because they did not pray, while Yehoshua and Calev, who had tefillah, succeeded.
The summer is not ownerless time: one must keep learning and keep the yoke of Heaven, and the open countryside is a chance to see Hashem's creation and join its song.
Those who fulfill their mission turn Tamuz and Av into days of joy and bring Moshiach.

title.en: The meraglim's failed mission and Yehoshua's spies

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how the meraglim set out on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz and returned forty days later on Tisha b'Av with a bad report, bringing weeping for all generations. He notes that Shlach is read before Tamuz and that its haftarah and the Midrash contrast them with the successful messengers sent by Yehoshua.

title.en: Why the world travels; every man a messenger

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why everyone starts travelling from Rosh Chodesh Tamuz, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on 'From Hashem are a man's steps established': every soul is sent down from the Kisei HaKavod on a mission to bring back mitzvos. Most people fail like Moshe's meraglim, while tzaddikim succeed like Yehoshua's messengers.

title.en: Each person's portion of creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adam's sin spoiled all of creation, and that each of his descendants has a portion of the world to repair or spoil; in the generation of the Flood even the animals were corrupted, while Noach's animals and his portion, Eretz Yisrael, were spared. He gives the Ba'al Shem Tov's example of a businessman sent to Chicago so he can make a brachah on a glass of water that has waited since creation.

title.en: The bochur's summer mission in the country

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the reasons people give for travelling are only excuses: a bochur who goes to the country is sent there for a tree to learn under, a brook to make a brachah on, a beis medrash to daven in, or a pool where he must behave with tznius. If he fulfills this he is like Yehoshua's messengers; the meraglim made these days into days of mourning, and those who fulfill their mission turn them into joy and bring Moshiach.

title.en: Guarding the eyes: Bilaam's blind eye

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that because the meraglim sinned with their eyes, these weeks are full of tests for the eyes, and the eyes are the holiest part of the body. He brings the Ba'al Shem Tov's reconciliation of Rashi and Onkelos on Bilaam 'shesum ha'ayin': only his blind eye, never defiled, could see prophecy; so too one who guards his eyes sees the light of Torah. He adds the mitzvah of tzitzis, which brings holiness into the eyes.

title.en: Tefillah for success in the mission

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must daven to Hashem to fulfill one's mission successfully, and tells of a tzaddik whose meticulous Pesach was spoiled by a grain of wheat in his soup; a dream-question revealed that he had not davened, and that a bird had dropped the kernel down the chimney. The meraglim failed for lack of tefillah, while Yehoshua, for whom Moshe davened, and Calev, who davened at Me'aras HaMachpelah, succeeded; from them come Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben Dovid.

title.en: Summer is not hefker: learning and kabbalas ol

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the summer months are hard for learning, yet they are not ownerless: a bochur may rest to gain strength, but must also learn in the summer and keep the yoke of Heaven, including in how he dresses. He tells of a bochur who threw off his yarmulke to run faster in a ball game, and contrasts him with one of the Slavita printers who stopped in the middle of running a gauntlet rather than go on without his yarmulke.

title.en: Joining creation's song; turning the months to joy

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rambam that a person comes to love and fear of Hashem by seeing the wonders of creation, which in the city are hidden but in the country are open to see; all creation sings to Hashem, and a Jew joins the song by learning, davening and avoiding aveiros. He closes that the meraglim made Tamuz and Av sad months, and those who fulfill their mission will turn them into joy, as Zechariah says, and Moshiach will point to them.

catalogTitle: This שבת Finalizes פורים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Parshas Parah, the Shabbos after Purim, continues Purim's lesson of a conduct above understanding, and that this is the merit through which Hashem can bring the Geulah in Nisan despite the Satan's accusations.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas Parah as the last Shabbos of the old year and explains that Haman erred in thinking Adar was the end, since for Jews the end touches the beginning. The sin of the Eitz HaDaas was the demand to understand everything; Parah Adumah, a chok that even Shlomo HaMelech could not understand, repairs it and partly atones for the Egel. Purim reflects Hashem's conduct with Jews as children, which is beyond reason, and Parah continues it. Turning to the year 5760, he explains the difference between a year fit for redemption and the fixed final time, describes how the Satan's accusations brought the decrees of Tach v'Tat and the world wars, and urges teshuvah. Parshas Parah, read before Nisan and before the three weeks, answers the Satan. Through the Gemara in Yoma about the race to the Mizbeach and the lottery, he shows that the goral reflects a conduct beyond merits. He closes with the higher purity of sprinkled water that comes from above.

en: For Jews time runs in a circle, so the end of the year touches its beginning; Haman, who rejoiced that his lot fell on Adar, did not understand this.
The sin of the Eitz HaDaas was the insistence on understanding everything, and Parah Adumah, a mitzvah kept without understanding, is its repair.
Hashem leads the Jews either as servants, according to their deeds, or as children, unconditionally; the miracle of Purim came through the conduct of children, which is above understanding.
When a time fit for Geulah arrives, the Satan accuses the Jews of their sins, and if they are not worthy, troubles come instead.
Parshas Parah is read before Nisan, a time of chesed, and Parshas Chukas before the three weeks, a time of rachamim, to answer the Satan's reasoning with a mitzvah done without reasons.
A goral reflects a conduct above merits; in the Beis HaMikdash a tie in the race showed that on that day the conduct was as children, so all the kohanim entered the lottery.
Parah Adumah brings a purity that comes from above, without the person's own act, and on Shabbos Parshas Parah Hashem grants every Jew a purity of the soul in preparation for Nisan.

candidateTopics: Parah Adumah as a chok beyond understanding
Hashem's conduct with Jews as children and as servants

title.en: The last Shabbos of the year and Haman's error

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Shabbos feeds the coming week and that Parshas Parah is the last Shabbos of the old year. Haman rejoiced that his lot fell on Adar, the end, but for Jews the end touches the beginning like a circle. He then defines the sin of the Eitz HaDaas as the wish to understand everything.

title.en: Parah Adumah, a mitzvah beyond understanding

summary.en: The Mashgiach presents Parah Adumah as the one mitzvah that teaches not to expect to understand, which even Shlomo HaMelech could not grasp. He explains that the Eitz HaDaas brought death, Matan Torah removed it, and the Egel, the same sin of wanting to understand, brought it back; Parah atones for the Egel partially by removing tumas meis.

title.en: Purim: Hashem's conduct with His children

summary.en: The Mashgiach distinguishes Hashem's two ways of leading the Jews, as servants and as children, and explains that the miracle of Purim came not through merit but because Jews are children of Hashem. Since this bond is above reason, Purim calls for surrendering one's da'as, and Parah, which follows Purim, continues it.

title.en: A year fit for Geulah and the fixed time

summary.en: The Mashgiach defines emunah as believing what one does not understand and calls the year 5760 especially fit for Moshiach. Through the passuk 'b'itah achishenah' he distinguishes years that are fit for Geulah from the fixed final time that no prophet may know, which was hidden even from Yaakov Avinu, and he explains that at every such time the Satan accuses the Jews.

title.en: Missed years of redemption and the call to teshuvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the decrees of Tach v'Tat, the Malbim's calculation for 1914 when the First World War began, and the expectation for the year Tav-Shin when the Second World War started, which he remembers from his boyhood. He points to this year's many tragedies as signs of the Satan's accusation and calls for Torah, teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

title.en: Parah answers the Satan before Nisan and the three weeks

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Satan argues there is no reason to bring Moshiach, and the answer is a mitzvah that itself has no reason, Parah. Nisan, a time of Geulah through chesed, and the three weeks, a time of rachamim through the Churban, are each preceded by the reading of Parah, so that Hashem may bring the Geulah without reasons.

title.en: The goral and the race to the Mizbeach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Purim miracle came through a goral, which like a lottery win cannot be explained. He brings the Gemara in Yoma on the kohanim racing up the Mizbeach and the lottery after a tie, and asks why all the kohanim enter the lottery and how a race could decide the avodah. From Koheles he answers that in the Beis HaMikdash there was no hester panim, so whoever reached first did so through merit.

title.en: A tie shows a day of children; Parah after Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how two kohanim can arrive together when no two Jews are on the same level, and answers that a tie shows that on that day Hashem was leading as with children, beyond merits, so a goral decides. Parshas Parah, the Shabbos after Purim, uses this same root of the goral before Nisan, and he begins to distinguish purity of the body from purity of the soul.

title.en: Purity sprinkled from above

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that whoever hears Parshas Parah receives a purity of the soul from Hashem, preparing him for the Korban Pesach. He contrasts the mikveh, which requires one's own act and cannot remove tumas meis, with the water of Parah, sprinkled from above, which can, and he closes by asking listeners to stand ready with humility and teshuvah when the parshah is read.

catalogTitle: דרשה בלשון הקודש - משיח נטמן בימי בין המצרים - והעבודה לגלותו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that under the orlah of the days of bein hamtzarim lies hidden the light of Moshiach, and that the work of every Jew, and especially of bochurim, is to remove that orlah from his heart through Torah, guarding the eyes and good middos.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a question on Parshas Pinchas: why does the division of the land put Menashe before Ephraim and stress that Reuven is the firstborn, when the order of the degalim had changed? He then shows that bein hamtzarim hides great light under an orlah. Balak, a great klipah, carried the root of Moshiach through Ruth, so a parsha bears his name, and his own korbanos brought the salvation. Pinchas, who becomes Eliyahu, will remove the orlah from the whole world. The three weeks are the orlah of time. Tammuz and Av, the months of Reuven and Shimon, fell with them and will be first in the order of tikkun, which answers the opening question. He calls on the bochurim of Shiloh to remove the orlah of the heart through Torah and guarding the eyes, and closes with the hope that the fasts become festivals.

en: The three weeks are not only heavy days: they hold great lights, even Moshiach's birth on Tisha b'Av, covered by an orlah of mourning.
Wherever great tumah is found, it is a sign that great holiness lies beneath it.
Balak's korbanos, brought to destroy Israel, earned him Ruth and the root of Moshiach: the trouble itself becomes the salvation.
Pinchas, who becomes Eliyahu, is the angel of both the individual bris and the great milah that will remove the orlah from the whole world.
In bein hamtzarim the Torah returns to the order of tikkun, the birth order in which Reuven, Shimon and Menashe come first.
The task of every Jew in these days is to remove the orlah from his heart; when Israel does so below, Hashem removes the orlah from the world.
The bochurim of Shiloh carry the kedushah of Yosef, holiness of the eyes, which they must guard especially in Tammuz and Av.

candidateTopics: Moshiach hidden in the three weeks
order of the tribes and the months
Shiloh and the kedushah of Yosef

title.en: Menashe before Ephraim in Pinchas

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah lists Menashe before Ephraim when dividing the land, though Yaakov put Ephraim first, and why Pinchas repeats that Reuven is the firstborn after the order of the degalim had changed. He notes that the parshiyos from Balak onward are the parshiyos of bein hamtzarim.

title.en: Why Balak merited a parsha

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Nechemiah did not merit a sefer named for him, and asks why the wicked Balak did. Beneath Balak lies hidden goodness: from him came Ruth and the root of Moshiach. He adds the Rambam's proof of Moshiach from Parshas Balak and the Midrash that Moshiach was born on Tisha b'Av.

title.en: Great tumah hides great holiness

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets a rule: great tumah is a sign of holiness beneath it, as the bris is covered by orlah and as the Chazon Ish wrote of a troubled bochur. He applies it to Chevron and Shechem, the places of milah, and to bein hamtzarim, days in which, as the Maggid of Mezritch and the students of the Ba'al Shem Tov taught, a great hidden light can be reached.

title.en: Balak's korbanos and the root of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Balak saw that Moshiach would come from him and therefore wanted to destroy Israel. He reads 'ben Tzipor' as an allusion to Moshiach and shows that the very korbanos Balak brought to curse Israel earned him Ruth. From the pasuk 'es tzarah hi l'Yaakov u'mimenah yivashea' and the Arizal he concludes that the trouble itself is the salvation.

title.en: Even the wicked serve Hashem's honor

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Pharaoh had a merit, since through him came kiddush Hashem at the Yam Suf, and the pasuk that Hashem made everything for His sake, even the wicked. He brings the Gemara on learning not for its own sake from Balak's korbanos, and Michah's call to remember what Balak advised. He reads 'yoshev mimuli' as Balak's fear that Israel would cut off his orlah, and turns to Pinchas.

title.en: Pinchas, Eliyahu and the milah of the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings two midrashim on Pinchas's 'bris shalom': that he becomes Eliyahu, herald of the geulah, and that he becomes the angel of the bris at every milah. He reconciles them: milah is both individual and general, the removal of orlah from the whole world, of which Esav is the root. He then shows from Sefer Yetzirah that the three weeks are the orlah of time, with hidden light beneath, which is why Eliyahu appears on Shabbos Pinchas.

title.en: Two orders of the tribes; Tammuz and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the tribes have an order of tikkun, by birth, and an order of kilkul, the degalim after the sin, in which Reuven lost his place. Every month corresponds to a tribe; Reuven and Shimon, fourth and fifth in the degalim, are Tammuz and Av, and when they fell, these months fell into the klipos. In the future every kilkul will return to its tikkun.

title.en: Aharon's stones and Reuven's holiness

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that even after the egel, the names on Aharon's shoulder stones follow the birth order, because Aharon, who enters the Kodesh HaKodashim, represents Israel in its state of tikkun. He explains the holiness of Reuven, Yaakov's first strength, and says that Tammuz and Av, the months of Reuven and Shimon, will in the future be raised above all months.

title.en: The opening question answered; Balak's hidden number

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers his opening question: in bein hamtzarim the Torah speaks of dividing the land in the order of tikkun, so Reuven is the firstborn and Menashe comes before Ephraim. He returns to Balak, whose parsha is named for the hidden good in him, and explains the importance of gematria and the milui, the hidden part of a letter's name, which in Balak points to Moshiach.

title.en: Removing the orlah of the heart

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the task of every Jew whom Hashem has touched in these days is to remove the orlah from his heart, as the Torah says 'u'maltem es orlas levavchem'; when Israel does this, Hashem removes the orlah from the world. He tells the bochurim they are Israel's true army, and that the miracles seen in the wars with the Arabs and the Gulf War came through the protection of Torah.

title.en: Jerusalem is decided in heaven

summary.en: The Mashgiach says everything revolves around Jerusalem, and that no prime minister decides what will be there: Hashem judges the princes above before the kings below. The strife over Jerusalem below is a sign of a judgment in heaven, perhaps that the time has come for Jerusalem to return, with the nations' angels accusing. The answer, he says, is teshuvah: the Torah of the bochurim and tzedakah, through which Moshiach will come.

title.en: Shabbos Chazon and the third Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Kedushas Levi that on Shabbos Chazon Hashem shows every Jew the third Beis HaMikdash, and shows that the hidden letters of 'Tisha b'Av' hint to the third Beis HaMikdash. He explains from the Zohar that Shabbos mincha is the highest time, and that the Shabbosos of bein hamtzarim, especially Shabbos Chazon, are wholly like it; each one reaches it according to his preparation during the week.

title.en: Shiloh, Yosef and guarding the eyes

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the bochurim that learning in Shiloh shows their souls belong to Shiloh and to the kedushah of Yosef, holiness of the eyes. He brings the Gemara that in Shiloh kodashim were eaten wherever it could be seen, unlike Jerusalem, and explains that Tammuz and Av are the two eyes. In the time of ikvesa d'Meshicha the bochurim must guard their eyes, especially in these months; he adds that Shiloh is the place of zivugim and that Hashem and Knesses Yisrael are the chassan and kallah.

title.en: Sefer Bamidbar ends with a wedding

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that entering the nine days we finish Bamidbar, which ends with the marriages of the daughters of Tzelafchad, and brings Tosafos in Gittin that there is no gap between Bamidbar and Devarim: there is no divorce, rather a holy zivug. Devarim opens with rebuke as a badchan rebukes a chassan before the chuppah. He closes that Tisha b'Av will become a festival, that the knife to remove the orlah is in the bochurim's hands, and with a tefillah for the geulah.

catalogTitle: התהפכות של חדשי תמוז ואב

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that Tammuz and Av, months of harsh judgment and churban, hide under their kelipah the greatest light of Moshiach, and that through toiling in Torah one can cut away that covering and turn the curse into a blessing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Tammuz as a month of strong judgment, the reversed form of Hashem's name, tied to the meraglim and to the tribes of Reuven and Shimon. Yet the navi Zechariah promises that these fasts will become days of joy, and he brings hints that redemption is born in them: Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', Boaz's wedding to Ruth on 17 Tammuz, and Moshiach's birth on Tisha b'Av. The rule is that the greater the kedushah, the thicker its orlah. The three nations not yet conquered, Amon, Moav and Edom, and Balak, ancestor of Moshiach who tried to hold him captive, show the same pattern in place and in soul; Tammuz and Av show it in time. Hashem turned Bilaam's curse into a blessing, and so a struggling bochur should know his thick orlah hides a great soul. Like Osniel ben Kenaz, who conquered by restoring forgotten halachos, one conquers these days through learning, guarding the eyes, and fulfilling one's shlichus without fear.

en: Tammuz and Av are months of strong judgment, linked to the sin of the meraglim and to tribes and nesi'im who stumbled.
According to Zechariah the fasts of the fourth and fifth months will become days of joy, and these days already carry the roots of redemption.
The greater a kedushah, the thicker the kelipah or orlah that surrounds it, like the orlah over the bris and the harsh nations of Eretz Yisrael.
Balak was the ancestor of Moshiach through Ruth, and as a great kelipah he tried to keep Moshiach captive within himself.
Each part of Eretz Yisrael holds a part of the Torah, so conquering it means revealing its halachos, and learning Torah in Tammuz and Av conquers these days.
Tammuz and Av correspond to the eyes, and guarding the eyes prepares a person to see the hidden light of the Torah.
Every Jew is a shliach of Hashem, and these months call on the bochurim to fulfill their shlichus without fear, as Kalev and Pinchas did.

title.en: Tammuz, a month of strong judgment

summary.en: After a word of thanks, the Mashgiach explains that Tammuz carries Hashem's name in reverse order and is a month of harsh judgment, harsher than Av. He links the month to Reuven, who was not blessed by Yaakov, and to the two nesi'im who stumbled, at Korach's congregation and at the deed of Zimri.

title.en: Days of churban destined to be festivals

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the days from the sending of the meraglim as low days of churban, then brings Zechariah's promise that the fasts will turn to joy. He adds Aharon's 'chag laHashem machar', the Chasam Sofer's reckoning that Boaz married Ruth on 17 Tammuz, and the Midrash that Moshiach is born on Tisha b'Av.

title.en: Great kedushah, thick orlah

summary.en: The Mashgiach states the rule that the greater the kedushah, the stronger the kelipah guarding it, as with the orlah over the bris and the harsh nations of Eretz Yisrael, and applies it to Tammuz and Av. He tells how the Plantcher Rebbe made a kind of kiddush on Tisha b'Av, saying it will be a Yom Tov when Moshiach comes.

title.en: The three nations Moshiach will conquer

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that of the ten nations promised to Avraham, Yehoshua conquered seven, while Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, Amon, Moav and Edom, await Moshiach. Moshe's conquest of Sichon and Og in the Tammuz parshiyos was only a beginning, and the Mashgiach calls on serious Jews to break the kelipah of these months, whose parshiyos all herald redemption.

title.en: Balak, grandfather of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts Nechemiah, who lost a sefer in his name, with Balak, who merited a parsha because his korbanos brought Ruth into the world. Balak sensed Moshiach would come from him and as a great kelipah tried to hold him back; the Ohr HaChaim reads 'ben Tzipor' as a hint to Moshiach, the bird waiting in its heavenly chamber.

title.en: Place, soul and time: the hidden Moshiach

summary.en: Using the Sefer Yetzirah idea that whatever exists in time also exists in soul and place, the Mashgiach sets Balak as the soul, Amon and Moav as the place and Tammuz and Av as the time where Moshiach lies hidden under an orlah. He brings 'v'hu yoshev mimuli', the Gemara's two doves, Ruth and Naamah, and the Rambam that Moshiach must come from David and Shlomo.

title.en: Curse turned to blessing; Osniel's conquest

summary.en: From 'vayahafoch Hashem Elokecha lecha es haklalah livrachah' the Mashgiach tells the bochur who struggles that a thick orlah is a sign of a great soul beneath it, to be cut away with teshuvah, hasmadah, tefillah and middos. He then explains how Osniel ben Kenaz conquered Kiryas Sefer by restoring through pilpul the halachos forgotten after Moshe's passing, since each part of Eretz Yisrael holds a part of the Torah.

title.en: Conquering Tammuz and Av through Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies this to the present: whoever sits and learns with iyun in Tammuz and Av, bringing out halachos, conquers a part of Eretz Yisrael and may help free Moshiach, as Moshe conquered Sichon and Og through his toil in Torah. He brings that 'haklalah livrachah' equals talmud Torah in gematria, the Avodas Yisroel that in bein hametzarim one can reach the Shechinah, and 'ki rabim bnei shomemah' about the souls of the last generations.

title.en: The eyes of Tammuz and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes today's new kelipos, the internet and the cell phone, that take the power of chiddush away from Torah, and says Torah must be earned to reveal its hidden light. Since Tammuz and Av correspond to the eyes, he calls for guarding the eyes, so that they can see the ohr haganuz of the Torah.

title.en: Months of shlichus; the call to the bochurim

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Tammuz and Av months of shlichus: the meraglim failed in theirs, while Kalev and Pinchas succeeded, and every Jew is sent by Hashem on a shlichus. The months beg the bochurim to redeem them through learning, as pidyon shevuyim, to go without fear like Kalev who davened in Chevron, and he closes with a brachah that the two months turn to blessing.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that parshiyos are joined only at times that call for repairing the sin of baseless hatred, and that each group of Jews may keep its own way as a family, not as a party, while loving every Jew.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with parshas Masei, which repeats Aharon's passing and adds that it was on Rosh Chodesh Av. Aharon, the Kohen Gadol, embodied the Beis Hamikdash, so his passing is a churban, read on the Shabbos that blesses Av. He then explains that every Jew is a letter of the Torah and that souls come in families, like the sedros of the year, each with its own Shabbos and each shevet with its own nusach. Yet at times of hoped-for redemption or of repairing baseless hatred, in Nissan, Tishrei, Sefirah and the Three Weeks, two parshiyos are joined. Through Kamtza and Bar Kamtza he shows how two people making peace could have saved Yerushalayim. Praising the refinement he finds in Stolin, he warns that chassidus must be a family, not a party, and closes with Aharon, the lover of peace, and the call to strengthen brotherhood in the month of Av.

en: Aharon the Kohen Gadol embodied the Beis Hamikdash, so the Torah's mention of his passing on Rosh Chodesh Av speaks of the churban.
Every Jew is a letter of the Torah, and souls belong to families, as each sedra has its own Shabbos and each shevet its own nusach.
Parshiyos are joined only before Nissan and Tishrei, in Sefirah and in the Three Weeks, the times of hoped-for geulah or of repairing baseless hatred.
Had Kamtza and Bar Kamtza made peace, two people could have tipped all of Yerushalayim to merit and prevented the churban.
Chassidus must be a family, not a party: a party says the truth is only with me, a family knows the other is also a family.
Aharon, lover and pursuer of peace, is the Beis Hamikdash, and the work of the month of Av is to strengthen brotherhood among Jews.

title.en: Why Masei repeats Aharon's passing

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why parshas Masei repeats Aharon's passing, adding the date Rosh Chodesh Av, and why it says only that the Kenaani 'heard'. He answers that Aharon the Kohen Gadol was the Beis Hamikdash itself, so his passing is a form of churban.

title.en: Masei as galus; Aharon's years as the Mikdash

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the journeys of Masei hint at the four exiles and that every Jew passes through them by Divine providence; the parsha is read on the Shabbos before Av. He then maps Aharon's 123 years onto the Mishkan's thirty, twenty and ten amos, and says his passing on Rosh Chodesh Av is the root of Tisha B'Av.

title.en: Letters, families and separate shevatim

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that every Jew is a letter of the Torah and that souls come in families that were together at the Kisei Hakavod and at Sinai. As each sedra has its own Shabbos, each shevet has its own nusach and customs, yet good ways may flow from one shevet to another.

title.en: When parshiyos are joined

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed through baseless hatred, so at certain times unity must be stressed. Parshiyos are joined before Nissan and Tishrei, the months of geulah, and in Sefirah and the Three Weeks, to repair the lack of unity; at other times each Shabbos stands alone.

title.en: My nusach, and the other is also a shevet

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a Jew should have his own nusach and Rebbe, but must know that the other is also a shevet of Klal Yisroel. He brings the Divrei Chaim on a chassid who says only his Rebbe is a Rebbe, and the dispute of shlishi and shishi, going back to the sea arguing with Moshe at Krias Yam Suf.

title.en: Kamtza and Bar Kamtza

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how two people could destroy Yerushalayim. He brings the Maharal that they were a sign of baseless hatred, and adds that all souls form one rope, so a fault below pulls down above, and that one act can tip the whole world. Had the two made peace over a l'chaim, the churban would have been averted.

title.en: Refinement: Stolin and Yehuda

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why he speaks of this here: in Stolin people are refined. He brings that Yehuda left his pledge with Tamar rather than take it back, because he was a refined man, and through this the kingship of Yehuda and Moshiach came.

title.en: A family, not a party; Aharon and Av

summary.en: The Mashgiach says chassidus in some ways became a party, which the Ba'al Shem Tov never intended, and contrasts a party, which holds that only it has the truth, with a family. He returns to Aharon's passing and the Kenaani's hearing: Av corresponds to Shimon, the 'hearing' went into galus, and Aharon, lover of peace, brought Jews together.

title.en: Rosh Chodesh gatherings and the call for unity

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that when Av comes, Jews sit together at seudos to strengthen brotherhood and renew the beauty of chassidus as a family. He urges that one group could be the one to bring Moshiach, explains why he spoke, and closes with a brachah that Tisha B'Av turn to joy.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that every Nisan is an offshoot of the original Rosh Chodesh Nisan of Creation, which Hashem has tried to bring down again and again, and that a Jew should renew himself and pray that this Nisan be the one of the final redemption.

abstract.en: Opening with Parshas HaChodesh, the Mashgiach calls Nisan a month of pure chesed and love between Hashem and Klal Yisrael, which is why Shir HaShirim is said on Pesach. Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, meant to enter an everlasting Shabbos, but the Satan spoiled the plan; in human terms Hashem was disappointed. Like a soul returning as a gilgul or ibbur, that original Nisan came down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and was spoiled by the Eigel, and again at the Mishkan's inauguration, spoiled once more. The Nisan of the Geulah is still awaited. He urges bentching Rosh Chodesh Nisan with kavanah, staying away from machlokes and keeping a kosher Pesach. Pesach belongs to Avraham and binds a Jew to Hashem, as kareis on Pesach and milah shows. Through gematria he shows that matzah is 'three times Adam'. As nature renews itself in Nisan, a Jew should renew himself and crown Hashem.

en: The chesed felt in the world every Nisan is a byproduct of the real Nisan, the love of Hashem for Klal Yisrael like a groom for a bride.
Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan so that he would pass from Friday into an everlasting Shabbos, and the Satan's sin spoiled that original 'Nisan of Bereishis'.
Like a gilgul or an ibbur of a soul, the original Nisan was brought down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and at the inauguration of the Mishkan, and both times it was spoiled.
Klal Yisrael is still waiting for the original Nisan to come down once more as the Nisan of the Geulah.
Pesach belongs to Avraham Avinu and is the moment a Jew binds himself to Hashem, which is why kareis applies to the positive mitzvos of milah and korban Pesach.
Matzah carries kedushah like tzitzis made for the sake of the mitzvah, and its value is 'lechem' with the full spelling of Hashem's Name: three times the Adam of 'na'aseh adam'.
Since all of nature renews itself in Nisan, a Jew should renew himself too and resolve to become a true Adam.

title.en: Nisan, a month of chesed and love

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Parshas HaChodesh and describes Nisan as a month of pure chesed that is felt even in nature. He explains that this is a byproduct of the real Nisan, Hashem's love for Klal Yisrael like a groom's for a bride, which is why Shir HaShirim is said on Pesach.

title.en: The Nisan of Creation and its spoiling

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, the sixth day of Creation, to enter an everlasting Shabbos, and that the Satan spoiled this plan through the sin. He asks how one can speak of Hashem being disappointed and answers that this is only how humans can describe it.

title.en: Gilgul and ibbur: a soul that returns

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Hashem decided to bring the original Nisan down again, and explains the difference between a gilgul and an ibbur, where a tzaddik's soul enters a person to help him. He illustrates it with an unexpectedly elevated Shabbos after the mikveh and with the story of the Arizal standing up for Rabbi Chaim Vital.

title.en: The second try: Nisan of Yetzias Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that place, time and soul all mirror each other, so an ibbur exists in place and in time too, as when the kedushah of Yerushalayim came to the Jews in the desert. The Nisan of Bereishis came down again at Yetzias Mitzrayim and rose until the Eigel spoiled it and death returned.

title.en: The Mishkan, and the Nisan still awaited

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the third try, the Nisan of the Mishkan's inauguration that is read about this week, which would have restored the state of Adam before the sin but was also spoiled. He stresses that Hashem never truly fails, and that the original Nisan will come down once more as the Nisan of the Geulah.

title.en: Bentching Rosh Chodesh Nisan; avoiding machlokes

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks that Rosh Chodesh Nisan be bentched this Shabbos with full kavanah, that it be the promised Nisan of the Geulah, especially in the year 5760. He warns at length to have no part in the current machlokes, and to learn, daven, give tzedakah, keep Shabbos and make a kosher Pesach.

title.en: Pesach, Avraham Avinu and the bond of matzah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Pesach is the yom tov of Avraham Avinu, as Shavuos is Yitzchak's and Sukkos Yaakov's, and that through Pesach a Jew becomes a Jew and binds himself to Hashem. This is why only milah and korban Pesach carry kareis among positive mitzvos, and why matzah, baked for the sake of the mitzvah, is filled with kedushah like tzitzis.

title.en: Matzah: three times Adam

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows that lechem is 78, three times Hashem's Name, and that matzah is the same 'lechem' with the full spelling of the Name, three times 45, the gematria of Adam. Eating matzah with kavanah and emunah fulfills 'na'aseh adam' at least in the individual, and he adds that there is far more to every mitzvah than appears on the surface.

title.en: Renew yourself; crown Hashem as King

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes how all of nature comes back to life in Nisan and sings to Hashem, and calls on each Jew not to sit back but to renew himself and resolve to become an Adam, as everything is new on Pesach. He closes with Nisan as the new year for kings and the roshei teivos of Hashem's Name, and prays that this Nisan be the Nisan of the Geulah.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Three Weeks are the hidden, still-unconquered 'territory of Esav' in time, that Shabbos Chazon already lets every Jew see the future consolation, and that shemittah, like Shabbos and Yerushalayim, makes every Jew a kohen who lives on Hashem's blessing.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Moshe's rebuke over the white manna: white draws down chessed, free sustenance like an infant's milk. Moshe prayed to enter 'the good mountain and the Levanon', the place of whiteness, against the red din of Edom. Hashem told him to turn 'tzafonah', to the hidden Torah. The ten nations promised to Avraham include three still unconquered, Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, which correspond to the Three Weeks, the boundary of Esav in time; therefore simcha cannot yet enter, and Shabbos Chazon is the highest of them. Yet Shabbos, with its tosefes, reaches past that boundary, so every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash. Moshe's conquest of Sichon and Og earned him Sefer Devarim, the 'Shabbos' and shemittah of the Torah. The Mashgiach then develops Shabbos, shemittah and Yerushalayim as one idea: nobody owns, Hashem gives, every Jew becomes a kohen. He ends with the three who said 'eicha' and Shabbos Chazon as an aufruf before the great wedding.

en: White draws down chessed: the manna was white because the generation of the desert received its sustenance freely, like an infant, outside the curse of 'by the sweat of your brow'.
The three unconquered nations, Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, correspond to the Three Weeks, which are Esav's boundary in time; simcha cannot yet be brought into them.
Shabbos, the source of blessing and of tosefes, can enter Esav's boundary, so on Shabbos Chazon every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash and the consolation of Tzion.
Sefer Devarim, Moshe's own part of the Torah, is the seventh book, the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah, earned through conquering Sichon and Og, the tosefes of Eretz Yisroel.
Shemittah teaches that Hashem, not man, is the owner; Yerushalayim, which was never divided among the tribes, is a constant shemittah, and in the seventh year it spreads over all of Eretz Yisroel.
In the shemittah year every Jew becomes like a kohen whose inheritance is Hashem: he lifts his eyes from the earth, learns Torah and trusts that sustenance comes from Hashem.

In the future all Jews will be kohanim, all of Eretz Yisroel will be Yerushalayim, and the whole world a day that is entirely Shabbos; great souls like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Eliyahu already live in that state.

title.en: Why the white manna drew Moshe's rebuke

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with Moshe's rebuke over the complaint about the white manna and explains that each color draws down a different light; white draws chessed, as seen in white garments of doctors and kohanim. Like an infant's white milk, the manna was white because the desert generation received free sustenance outside the curse of 'by the sweat of your brow'.

title.en: The Levanon against the redness of Edom

summary.en: Moshe asked how they could complain about food given in chessed, and then himself prayed in chessed to enter 'the good mountain and the Levanon', the Beis HaMikdash, the place of whiteness. Edom is red, the side of din; the Mashgiach contrasts Esav's craving for red with the future when Hashem comes from Edom in red garments.

title.en: Turn north: the hidden Torah and the heel generation

summary.en: Moshe is told 'turn northward', which the Mashgiach reads as turning to the Torah, called 'tzafun', hidden. Esav's land is not given 'until the sole of the foot': not the great generations of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and Rabbi Akiva but the lowest generation, the heel of Moshiach, will merit judging Mount Esav, and the three last nations promised to Avraham.

title.en: Three matzos, three nations, three weeks

summary.en: The three matzos under the Seder plate correspond to Keini, Kenizi and Kadmoni, that is Ammon, Moav and Seir; Moshe, the middle matzah, reached Moav, while Seir awaits Moshiach. The seven conquered nations correspond to the seven weeks of consolation, which are within reach, while the three hidden ones correspond to the Three Weeks, the greatest Shabbosos of the year whose light is still beyond grasp.

title.en: Esav's boundary in time: no simcha yet

summary.en: Seir refused to let Moshe pass, because Esav does not yet concede the blessings to Yaakov, and 'I will not give you of their land'. The same boundary exists in time: the Three Weeks, with Shabbos Chazon as Kadmoni, their highest, are Esav's province, where one may not bring in Yisroel's simcha; therefore tzaddikim said even a smile on Tisha b'Av is dangerous, while Yerushalayim is the source of all simcha.

title.en: Shabbos Chazon: every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: Shabbos is different: the satan has no hold on it, and like the matzah eaten on Shabbos erev Pesach it gives a measure of grasp even now. The Mashgiach brings the teaching attributed to the Kedushas Levi that on Shabbos Chazon every Jew sees the third Beis HaMikdash, with the parable of the father who shows his son a third, beautiful garment, and explains 'chazon' as seeing with the heart.

title.en: Shabbos as source of blessing and tosefes

summary.en: From the Pri Tzaddik: the blessings of the week lie in its Shabbos, and since Tisha b'Av is the birth of Moshiach, that birth already lies in Shabbos Chazon. Shabbos is the source of blessing, and blessing means increase; tosefes Shabbos spreads beyond its borders, which is why Shabbos can enter Esav's boundary. The Three Weeks are days of 'orlah' covering a great holiness, the Name hidden in 'mi ya'aleh lanu hashamaymah'.

title.en: Removing the orlah: Torah conquers Eretz Yisroel

summary.en: The seven nations were an orlah covering Eretz Yisroel, so the land was promised in the parsha of milah and Yehoshua circumcised the people before entering. Osniel ben Kenaz conquered Kiryas Sefer and through his pilpul restored the forgotten halachos hidden there; so every piece of Torah learned with toil conquers a part of Eretz Yisroel. The land of Sichon and Og, given to Gad and Reuven, is the tosefes, 'chelkas mechokek', Moshe's portion.

title.en: Sefer Devarim: the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah

summary.en: Following the Pri Tzaddik, Sefer Devarim stands between the Written and Oral Torah: Moshe said it on his own and was then told to write it. He merited it after conquering Sichon and Og; counting 'Vayehi binso'a' as a separate book, Devarim is the seventh book, the Shabbos and shemittah of the Torah. Moshe then thought the world had reached Shabbos and the decree was annulled, since shemittah, like Shabbos, has a tosefes.

title.en: Shabbos, shemittah and Yerushalayim: nobody is owner

summary.en: As the six weekdays prepare for Shabbos, Eretz Yisroel prepares for Yerushalayim, whose produce is brought there; Yerushalayim is the moon and malchus, with nothing of its own. Shemittah teaches that Hashem is the owner, as Shabbos teaches that Hashem creates; Yerushalayim, where nothing is planted and which was not divided among the tribes, is always shemittah, and in the seventh year spreads over the whole land. Both are for the poor, and for sitting and learning.

title.en: The shemittah Jew becomes a kohen

summary.en: After shemittah one goes up to Yerushalayim to learn; the true 'festival of gathering' is the gathering of Torah and of Yisroel, Hashem's harvest. A farmer looks down to the earth for his crop, but shemittah tells him to lift his eyes, for his inheritance is Hashem; the Mashgiach announces that the shemittah year is now coming, when every Jew should become a kohen who learns and trusts in Hashem.

title.en: Twelve tribes, Yaakov and the future kingdom of kohanim

summary.en: Eretz Yisroel was divided into twelve portions like the twelve months; Yaakov, above the tribes, is Shabbos, and Yerushalayim is his city. So on weekdays one asks twelve blessings in Shemoneh Esrei, but on Shabbos one middle blessing for being a Shabbos Jew. In the future Yerushalayim will spread over the land, all Jews will be a kingdom of kohanim, and there will be white, the Levanon, not Esav's red.

title.en: Eating 'atika': Shabbos meal and shemittah

summary.en: On 'what will we eat in the seventh year' the Torah answers 'you will eat the old', which the Targum renders 'atika', as on Shabbos one eats the meal of Atika Kadisha; the Mashgiach tells of the Beis Aharon and a simple chassid who relished Shir HaShirim without knowing its meaning. Some great souls, like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai whom the Zohar calls Shabbos, live in constant shemittah; hence his view in Berachos and the halacha following him in Maseches Shabbos.

title.en: Eliyahu the kohen in the cemetery

summary.en: In the future the halacha will follow Rabbi Shimon; Shabbos and Yerushalayim need no sanctification by a court, and shemittah is forgiveness. The Mashgiach tells how Rabbah bar Avuha found Eliyahu in a non-Jewish cemetery and asked whether he was not a kohen; Eliyahu answered with Rabbi Shimon's view. Since Eliyahu, of the tribe of Gad, already lives in the days of Moshiach when all Jews are kohanim, he answered by the halacha of that time.

title.en: Three who said 'eicha': Shabbos Chazon as an aufruf

summary.en: The Midrash says three prophets said 'eicha', Moshe, Yeshayahu and Yirmiyahu, and all three come together on Shabbos Chazon in the parsha, haftarah and Eicha; they are the shoshvinin who lead to the wedding in Yerushalayim, so Shabbos Chazon is an aufruf. The Mashgiach closes that one should use this Shabbos to sew the garments, accept the yoke of kehunah, Torah and bitachon for the shemittah year, and merit the garments of the redemption.

oneLiner.en: On the yahrzeit of the Arizal, the Mashgiach says that the counsel for the last generation is tefillah, and calls for lively, united davening together with the chazzan.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only to our eyes: its kedushah remains, as the Rambam rules about the holiness of the Temple site, and Tisha B'Av was meant to be a great Yom Tov. He then explains that in earlier generations a person's tefillah was weighed by his Torah, while in a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the state of the generation. He notes that davening has recently weakened and calls for lively davening, together with the chazzan, like the angels who sing as one, and with a raised voice that the Shulchan Aruch says awakens kavanah. Turning to the Arizal's yahrzeit, he says the Arizal came down to guide the last generation, and he brings the Toldos Aharon Rebbe's lively davening. A story of Mordechai's fast over Pesach leads to a reason for quiet davening on Tisha B'Av. He ends that whatever is weak needs chizuk, and that learning and davening pull each other.

en: The Mashgiach says the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only as it appears to us; its kedushah remains, as the Rambam rules about the Temple site.
In a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the state of the generation, not by the measure of earlier, Torah-filled times.
The Mashgiach calls for lively davening, together with the chazzan, so that each person feels part of the whole of Klal Yisroel, like the angels who sing as one.
The Arizal, whose teachings were for great mekubalim, also came down to guide the last generation, and the counsel for that generation is tefillah.
Whatever area of avodah has weakened needs chizuk, and learning and davening each pull the other along.

title.en: The kedushah of the Mikdash and tefillah today

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed only to our eyes, that its kedushah remains as the Rambam rules, and that Tisha B'Av was meant to be a great Yom Tov. He then explains that in a weak generation Hashem accepts tefillah according to the generation's state.

title.en: Lively davening, all together

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that davening has weakened and calls for lively tefillah together with the chazzan, like the angels who sing as one. He says this united tefillah is the one the Arizal spoke of for the last generation, and brings the Shulchan Aruch that a raised voice awakens kavanah.

title.en: The Arizal's yahrzeit and his guidance

summary.en: On the Arizal's yahrzeit the Mashgiach says one connects to him through his Torah, and that the Arizal also came down to guide the last generation. He tells how the Toldos Aharon Rebbe urged lively davening even on Tisha B'Av, and says that we must follow the Shulchan Aruch.

title.en: Mordechai's fast, Tisha B'Av, and chizuk

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a story of Mordechai's fast over Pesach and suggests from it a reason for quiet davening on Tisha B'Av. He then explains that whatever has weakened needs chizuk, that learning and davening pull each other, and closes on the joy in heaven at a gathering of chizuk on the Arizal's yahrzeit.

catalogTitle: ב - ה' מנ"א תשל"ח - אמונה בתורת הסוד וביאור שנטמן האר"י הק' בימים אלו.
zman: מסיבת לחיים בקעמפ תורה ודעת דרשה אחר שריפה במחנה תורה ודעת (קעמפ)

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that in a long galus Jews are judged by their emunah alone, and that the hidden light of the Nine Days, the days of the Arizal's passing, calls for believing in the secrets of the Torah even without understanding them.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach contrasts two nearly identical verses in Tehillim about Hashem coming to judge the world: if Moshiach comes early, Jews are judged by the measure of Torah; if galus drags on past kitz after kitz, they are judged by their emunah. Like watchmen waiting for morning, Jews keep hoping, and so Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on 'a tzaddik lives by his emunah'. On the Arizal's day of passing, he says the Arizal's words cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh, so at his tziyun one can only sing his zemiros. The Arizal and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai share one soul and passed away in days of mourning, whose light is too great for now and appears as darkness. Rabbi Shimon revealed open and hidden Torah, so his day is a joy; the Arizal's stays hidden. The Mashgiach ends by urging everyone to believe his emunah is whole.

en: The quality of Klal Yisrael is to keep waiting for the morning of the geulah, like watchmen, even after many kitzim and disappointments.
Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on emunah because his prophecy was for a generation that had fallen so low that emunah is what it can hold on to.
When the galus is long, Hashem judges the Jewish people by their emunah, not by the great Torah and avodah of earlier generations.
The Arizal's teachings cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh; at his tziyun one can at least sing his zemiros.
Days of mourning such as the Nine Days hide a light so great that it appears as darkness, kept for the tzaddikim in the future.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai revealed both the revealed and hidden Torah, so his day is joyous; the Arizal revealed only the hidden, so his day stays concealed.
Every Jew has a hidden point in his heart that believes in Hashem, and he should believe that his emunah is whole even when doubts arise.

candidateTopics: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and the Arizal

title.en: Waiting for the morning: emunah in a long galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach points to two similar verses about Hashem coming to judge the world, and says Moshiach can come early or after a long wait. Like watchmen waiting for morning, Jews keep hoping after every kitz that passed, and this is why Chavakuk based all the mitzvos on emunah for a fallen generation.

title.en: Judged by uprightness or by emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a navi's name carries his message, and Chavakuk's is clinging to emunah. Had Moshiach come in earlier generations, each Jew would have been judged by his Torah and avodah; now, after the kitzim passed, the verse says the nations will be judged by their emunah.

title.en: The Arizal's day: singing at his tziyun

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that today is the Arizal's yahrzeit and that his secrets cannot be understood without ruach hakodesh. He tells how at the Arizal's tziyun in Tzfas, unable to say over his teaching, he sang his zemiros, and explains that the Arizal and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai are one soul who both passed away in days of mourning.

title.en: Hidden light, hidden secrets, and complete emunah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the days of sefirah and the Nine Days hold a light kept for the future, too great for us now, so it appears as darkness; Rabbi Shimon revealed both nigleh and nistar, so his day is a joy, while the Arizal revealed only secrets, so his day stays hidden. Returning to the verse, he calls on everyone to strengthen his emunah, believe in the secrets hidden in the Torah, and believe that his own emunah is whole.

catalogTitle: The War Against עמלק & חמץ

oneLiner.en: On the eve of Rosh Chodesh Nissan, with Jewish soldiers fighting in Iraq, the Mashgiach explains that the days of the Nesi'im and the clearing out of chametz are Klal Yisrael's real war against Yishmael, Amalek and the yetzer hara.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a call from a former talmid, now an army chaplain on his way to Iraq, and urges the bochurim to daven and learn for the Jewish soldiers; learning and davening are the real weapons. He then turns to the minhag of reading the Nesi'im in the first twelve days of Nissan, and explains why a minhag can outweigh a halacha: a practice that all of Klal Yisrael takes on is a kind of prophecy that Hashem puts into their hearts. The Nesi'im of Yisrael stand against the twelve Nesi'im of Yishmael, and Rosh Chodesh Nissan, the new year for kings, is a day of great power. Chametz is the yetzer hara, rooted in Amalek, as the Radbaz answers from the Zohar; Avraham's war against the four kings on Pesach parallels the ways of destroying chametz. He ends with renewal: the whole of Nissan is like Rosh Chodesh, and one must leave atzvus behind and come to Hashem with simcha.

en: The Mashgiach says the bochurim must daven and learn seriously for the Jewish soldiers in Iraq, since learning and davening are the real fighting and a blatt Gemara is a weapon.
A minhag accepted by all of Klal Yisrael outweighs a halacha, because Hashem puts it into the hearts of the people as a kind of collective prophecy.
The twelve Nesi'im who brought the offerings for the dedication of the Mizbe'ach subdue the twelve Nesi'im of Yishmael, so reading the Nesi'im is a weapon against Yishmael.
Each of the first twelve days of Nissan governs one month of the year, and any ten Jews who daven with kavanah on Rosh Chodesh Nissan have a say in the heavenly court.
Chametz is the yetzer hara, which Amalek controls; this is why the Torah is stricter about chametz than about other aveiros.
Avraham Avinu's war on Pesach against the four kings, the four kingdoms of galus, corresponds to destroying chametz through the four elements.
All of Nissan carries the holiness of Rosh Chodesh, a time to renew oneself, and the atzvus that follows an aveirah is worse than the aveirah itself.

title.en: A chaplain's call and the war in Iraq

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a call from a former talmid, now an army chaplain heading to Iraq, who told him there are over a thousand Jewish soldiers there. He urges the bochurim to daven and learn for them, calling a blatt Gemara a 'MOAB' bomb and Amen yehei shmei rabba a Patriot missile.

title.en: The Shivas Yemei HaMilu'im and the Nesi'im

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the seven days of the Milu'im before Rosh Chodesh Nissan and the minhag of reading the Nasi of each day during the first twelve days of Nissan. Unlike Chanukah, where it is a takanah, in Nissan it is only a minhag, and some are lenient about it.

title.en: Why a minhag is greater than a halacha

summary.en: The Mashgiach says a minhag can override a halacha, giving the example of Hallel with a brachah on Rosh Chodesh, which Sefardim say without a brachah. He explains, citing the Kuzari, that a practice all of Klal Yisrael takes on is a prophecy Hashem puts into their hearts, from a higher source than a takanas Chazal.

title.en: Nesi'im against Yishmael; Rosh Chodesh Nissan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Nesi'im of Yisrael subdue the twelve Nesi'im of Yishmael, so reading them during the battle for Baghdad is a weapon. Rosh Chodesh Nissan is the new year for kings, when the Ba'al Shem Tov secluded himself; any ten Jews davening with kavanah have power above, and each of the twelve days governs a month.

title.en: Chametz is the yetzer hara, rooted in Amalek

summary.en: The Mashgiach says bein hazmanim is for helping prepare for Pesach and clearing out chametz, which is the yetzer hara controlled by Amalek. He brings the question why chametz is treated more strictly than other aveiros and the Radbaz's answer from the Zohar, then the story of Reb Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and the women kashering their dishes before Pesach.

title.en: Avraham's Pesach war and the four elements

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Ramban that Avraham's war against the four kings is the war against the four kingdoms of galus, and shows from the passuk and Rashi that it took place on Pesach. The four kings correspond to the four elements, and the ways of destroying chametz (burning, wind, water, bitul) use those elements; Avraham defeated them by throwing earth.

title.en: Renewal in Nissan, without atzvus

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Shelah that all of Nissan has the holiness of Rosh Chodesh, and calls for teshuvah and renewal as nature renews itself. He warns that the atzvus after an aveirah is worse than the aveirah, notes that Adam was created on Rosh Chodesh Nissan, and closes with a story about davening with simcha because 'we are Your children'.

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam's impure mouth could speak the holy blessings and prophecies of the days of Moshiach, and begins to explain it through the Gemara and the Ba'al Shem Tov's reading of Bilaam's blind eye.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the passuk that Hashem put a word in Bilaam's mouth. Bilaam had an impure mouth, yet he spoke the holy parshiyos of Bilaam: the great blessings and the prophecies about the days of Moshiach. How could such a mouth say such things? The Mashgiach explains that Hashem put something into his mouth that served as a barrier, so that the words would not come from Bilaam's own mouth. He brings the Gemara that Hashem placed a hook in his mouth, so that the words came out from that foreign thing and not from Bilaam's mouth. He then turns to the words 'shesum ha'ayin': Rashi explains that Bilaam's eye was blinded, while the Targum explains that he saw clearly, two opposite readings. The Ba'al Shem Tov reconciles them: Hashem made one of Bilaam's eyes blind so that he could not harm with it.

en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam, with his impure mouth, could speak the holy blessings and the prophecies of the days of Moshiach.
Hashem placed something in Bilaam's mouth as a barrier, so that the holy words came out of that foreign thing and not from his own mouth.
The Ba'al Shem Tov explains that Bilaam had one blind eye, made so by Hashem so that he could not do harm with it, which bridges Rashi's and the Targum's opposite readings of 'shesum ha'ayin'.

title.en: Holy words from Bilaam's impure mouth

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how Bilaam's impure mouth could speak holy blessings and prophecies, answers from the Gemara that Hashem put a hook in his mouth as a barrier, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov on Rashi's and the Targum's opposite readings of Bilaam's eye.

catalogTitle: בבית המדרש אמונת ישראל

oneLiner.en: At a l'chaim for the Ohr HaChaim, the Mashgiach explains that the Ohr HaChaim is a reflection of Moshiach, and reads his remez on the passuk 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' as describing Moshiach's longing for Klal Yisrael.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the tradition that the Ba'al Shem Tov, who had the nefesh of Moshiach, wished to meet the Ohr HaChaim, who had the ruach of Moshiach, and that their meeting would have brought the redemption, but it was held back from Heaven. He connects the Ohr HaChaim to the days around the Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day Moshe brought down the first luchos, a day that keeps a great power because in the world of tikkun every lost virtue returns. He then reads the Ohr HaChaim's remez on 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' in parshas Re'eh: the evyon is Moshiach, who longs for Klal Yisrael and wept on hearing that Jews await him; the passuk asks a Jew not to harden his heart, to share in Moshiach's longing, and to do every mitzvah with the intent of bringing him. He closes with three stories of the Ohr HaChaim.

en: The Mashgiach explains that the Ohr HaChaim is a reflection of Moshiach: the Ba'al Shem Tov said he himself had the nefesh of Moshiach and the Ohr HaChaim its ruach.
The Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day Moshe was to bring down the first luchos, still holds a great power, since in the world of tikkun every lost virtue returns.
Following the Ohr HaChaim, the 'evyon' of the passuk in Re'eh is Moshiach, who longs for Klal Yisrael like a pauper longs for what he lacks.
Not hardening one's heart means sharing in Moshiach's longing and having compassion on him.
With every good deed, whether tefillah, tefillin or a page of Gemara, a Jew should have in mind that he does it to bring Moshiach.

title.en: The Ohr HaChaim and the Seventeenth of Tammuz

summary.en: After a l'chaim, the Mashgiach brings the tradition that the Ba'al Shem Tov wished to meet the Ohr HaChaim, since together they held the nefesh and ruach of Moshiach. He then explains that the Seventeenth of Tammuz, the day of the first luchos, keeps a great power for the future tikkun, and that the words of the Ohr HaChaim can bring great awakenings.

title.en: Moshiach as the evyon of parshas Re'eh

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads the passuk 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon' with the Ohr HaChaim's remez that the evyon is Moshiach. He explains the name evyon as one who longs for what he lacks, brings Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's encounter in which Moshiach wept on hearing that Jews await him, and reads 'one of your gates' as Moshiach being the unique one of the Sanhedrin.

title.en: Teshuvah, a soft heart and every mitzvah for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a second reading: Chazal say that if one congregation does teshuvah Moshiach comes at once, and he explains that the teshuvah asked of each generation differs. From 'do not harden your heart' he explains that a Jew must feel compassion and share in Moshiach's longing, and with every mitzvah have in mind to bring Moshiach.

title.en: Stories of the Ohr HaChaim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells three stories: the Ohr HaChaim finding a Rambam hidden under a step in the Karaite synagogue in Yerushalayim, the lion that guarded him in the desert over Shabbos, and the Chida's account of Eliyahu HaNavi visiting him. He closes by saying that honoring the Ohr HaChaim, a reflection of Moshiach, should bring a strong longing for Moshiach.

catalogTitle: A Month of תחיית המתים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains Nisan as the month of revival, in which Hashem renews His plan for a perfect world again and again, and shows how matzah, as a key of chesed from a world above time and space, opens a Jew to that renewal.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens on Chaf-Hei Adar, recalling the Gemara's dispute whether the world was created in Tishrei or Nisan, and notes that Hashem's 'regret' is language for our understanding, since everything was in His plan. He then describes Nisan as a series of attempts at a perfect world: Adam HaRishon, Avraham Avinu the 'spring neshama' and Yetzias Mitzrayim spoiled by the Egel, the Mishkan spoiled by Nadav and Avihu, and a fourth Nisan of Moshiach that will succeed. From the Mishkan built and taken apart for seven days he draws the message never to despair after a fall. Nisan is a month of chesed, harnessed chesed, which he illustrates through the right hand, the lunar calendar balanced by the solar year, and Shabbos in the middle. Matzah is the key that opens the doors of chesed; its gematria of three times Mah shows it comes from a world above time and space, unlike bread. He closes with Pesach as the beginning, the bris of the Jew with Hashem, and a story about davening for a kosher Pesach.

en: Nisan is the month of renewal in which Hashem 'tries again' for a perfect world: with Adam HaRishon, with Yetzias Mitzrayim, with the Mishkan, and finally with Moshiach.
Avraham Avinu is the 'spring neshama' of Klal Yisroel, and the main events of his life took place on Pesach.
Nisan is a month of chesed, the midah of Avraham, but Jewish chesed is harnessed and balanced by din.
Matzah is the key that opens the doors of chesed and brachah on Pesach; Targum renders matzah as 'patira', opening.
Matzah comes from a world above time and space, which is why it may not be given time to rise, while bread depends on both.
Pesach is the beginning, the bris that ties a Jew to Hashem, so eating chametz brings kares, the opposite of that bond.
